LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights Plus, how to watch, what to know and a prediction before the 'Thursday Night Football' matchup Getty Images In the Week 11 edition of "Thursday Night Football," the Houston Texans play host to the division rival Indianapolis Colts . Houston enters this game coming off a dispiriting loss to the Cleveland Browns that dropped the Texans to just 3-6 on the season and dealt a significant blow to their playoff hopes. The Texans need to start stacking wins, and they need to do it right now if they want to make a run at a back-end postseason spot. The Colts, meanwhile, snapped a five-game losing streak with a close win over the Miami Dolphins last week. They didn't exactly light the world on fire, though, and have the look of a team that is just playing out the string after their series of trades ahead of the deadline. Will the Texans bounce back, or will the Colts make it two in a row? We'll find out soon enough. Before we break down the matchup, here's a look at how you can watch the game. Follow the game live here Where to watch Texans vs. Colts live Date: Thursday, Nov. 19 | Time: 8:15 p.m. ET Location: NRG Stadium (Houston) Streaming: Amazon Prime Follow: CBS Sports App Odds: Texans -12.5, O/U 44.5 via DraftKings Sportsbook When the Colts have the ball The Texans defense has been one of the most disappointing units in the league this season. Houston ranks 20th in yards allowed, 18th in points allowed and 22nd in EPA per play, according to Tru Media. The Texans checked in first in yards, second in scoring and third in EPA per play a year ago, and were expected to again field one of the top defenses in the league this season after returning almost all of their key pieces. Instead, Houston has struggled to contain opposing passing attacks, repeatedly leaking on the back end despite putting pressure on quarterbacks at an above-average rate. Players like Kamari Lassiter have regressed significantly, while Reed Blankenship has been a bust as a free-agent signing. Luckily for the Texans, they are about to face one of the most inept passing offenses in the NFL . Daniel Jones has been entirely unable to drive the ball in intermediate and deep areas of the field since returning from his Achilles tear, and it has neutered the entire aerial attack. Jones has completed a career-low 59.6% of his passes at a career-low 5.6 yards per attempt, with just seven touchdowns against a league-high 12 interceptions. The Colts also traded away both Josh Downs and Keenan Allen last week, leaving them with Laquon Treadwell , Ashton Dulin , Anthony Gould and Deion Burks as their main wide receivers. There is not an imposing player in the bunch. The Texans should be able to shut down this passing offense with relative ease -- especially if they can get pressure on Jones, who can no longer evade the rush like he did last season. He's already been sacked more times than he was a year ago despite playing three fewer games. The Colts have turned the dial down on Jonathan Taylor 's workload in recent weeks, having him split snaps and carries with rookie Seth McGowan , including in the red zone. Taylor played 81.2% of the offensive snaps through the Colts' first six games, according to Pro-Football Reference, but is at just 66.5% of the snaps since then, with McGowan's usage ticking up. Taylor has also not been as effective this season (career-low 4.2 yards per carry) as in recent years, which isn't surprising given the total lack of a passing game and the Colts' offensive line issues. Those issues should persist on Thursday, with both of Indianapolis' starting tackles out for this game. It's fairly difficult to run on the Texans to begin with (4.0 yards per carry allowed), and it should be even more so with the Colts in their current state. When the Texans have the ball C.J. Stroud is playing the best ball of his career, including his rookie year. Stroud checks in sixth in the NFL in EPA per dropback, according to Tru Media, despite the fact that he's been working with an injured and rotating pass-catcher corps for much of the season. The Colts are an easy bunch to throw on, checking in 27th in the league in net yards per attempt allowed (which accounts for sack yardage), and they won't have Charvarius Ward in this game and may not have Sauce Gardner , either. Nico Collins should see favorable matchups on the outside and be able to feast all night long. The likes of Tank Dell and Xavier Hutchinson could get in the mix as well, though they tend to rotate more heavily in and out of the lineup and therefore see fewer targets than Collins. It's also quite easy to run on Indy, which has leaked 4.8 yards per carry on the season, 29th in the NFL. The Texans, though, have been entirely unable to run the ball, with neither David Montgomery (who is set to return from injury on Thursday night) nor Woody Marks (who is out with a concussion) able to establish anything resembling success on the ground. Montgomery was averaging a mere 2.7 yards per carry before his injury, and Marks has been at only 3.7 per carry in Monty's absence. This is likely to be a game where the Texans lean heavily on Stroud to establish a lead, then turn to the ground game to run the clock out, in what should be a relatively easy matchup given the state of the Colts' roster. So long as the Texans keep Stroud well protected early on, that strategy should be plenty successful, even if it doesn't necessarily result in a blowout win because the Texans themselves aren't that explosive of an offense. I just don't think the Texans should be favored by 12.5 points over anybody. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin predict this weekend's top games Getty Images Last week in the NFL was full of drama. The Cleveland Browns came back from down 17-0 to defeat the Houston Texans , while Kirk Cousins was victorious in his first game back with the Minnesota Vikings . The San Francisco 49ers and Dallas Cowboys put up 86 total points in Arlington, and the Cincinnati Bengals blew out Aaron Rodgers and the Pittsburgh Steelers on "Sunday Night Football." This week there's more. Fernando Mendoza will make the first road start of his career against an aggressive Denver Broncos defense, the Detroit Lions will begin life without Aidan Hutchinson at home against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers , and the Vikings will play the 49ers in Mexico City in what could go down as one of the best primetime matchups of the entire season. There are many, many massive spreads in the NFL this week! Which teams should you pick in Week 11, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Nov. 18 over at DraftKings Sportsbook. Indianapolis Colts at Houston Texans (-12.5) (TNF) Dajani (Texans -12.5): I would typically lean toward a huge underdog like this in a divisional game, but two factors have me leaning the other way. One, Daniel Jones threw for just 108 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions last week against the Miami Dolphins . They were starting a quarterback that had never played in the NFL, yet only lost by two points. Jones has been terrible. He's turned the ball over an NFL-high 15 times and has the worst record in primetime by any quarterback since 1970 at 1-16. Additionally, the Texans allowed the Browns to come back from down 17-0 and win their meeting last week, which I imagine has this Texans team seeing red. C.J. Stroud and Co. are better than their 3-6 record indicates. They even beat the Jacksonville Jaguars earlier this season. I think the large number is justified. … Prediction: Texans 27, Colts 14 Dubin (Colts +12.5): I just don't think the Texans should be favored by 12.5 points over anybody. … Prediction: Texans 23, Colts 13 Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Detroit Lions (-7) Dajani (Buccaneers +7): Jahmyr Gibbs leads the NFL in rushing yards this season with 1,000, while the Buccaneers allow the fewest rushing yards per game (79.2). The Bucs also lead the NFL in rushing offense and in takeaways with 21. With the Buccaneers coming off their bye week and the Lions coming off an international trip that cost them Aidan Hutchinson for the season, I'm leaning toward Tampa Bay with the points. The Bucs are 4-1 against the spread in their last five games, but keep an eye on the quarterback situation over the next 24 hours. … Prediction: Lions 24, Buccaneers 21 Dubin (Lions -7): The Bucs likely playing this game without Baker Mayfield pushed me in this direction. Jalon Daniels is fine, but I don't expect the passing game to be able to do much here. The Bucs base the entire offense around the run anyway, but the Lions are actually pretty tough to run on. That could change without Aidan Hutchinson, obviously, but I don't think it will change enough for Tampa's offense to keep pace with what the Lions are likely to do. … Prediction: Lions 24, Buccaneers 16 Las Vegas Raiders at Denver Broncos (-10) Dajani (Broncos -10): I don't think Fernando Mendoza wins his second career start in an environment like Mile High, but can he cover the double-digit spread? Denver has won just one game by double digits this season, back in Week 7 against the Arizona Cardinals . The Las Vegas Raiders, on the other hand, have covered in four straight divisional games for the first time since 2022. The Broncos are coming off their bye week and have scored at least 26 points in each of their last three games. Bo Nix has also thrown multiple touchdowns in back-to-back games. The Raiders are tied for the worst scoring defense in the NFL this year with 28.9 points allowed per game, so I think the Broncos could reach 30 points this week. That could make it tough for Mendoza to cover the spread. He's actually the first rookie quarterback to ever face both of the previous season's No. 1 seeds in his first two career starts. … Prediction: Broncos 30, Raiders 17 Dubin (Raiders +10): The Broncos have seven wins this year, and six of them are by one score. The only team they beat by more than seven points is the Cardinals. I reserve the right to change this pick if Brock Bowers is out and Fernando Mendoza just doesn't have anyone at all to throw the ball to, but otherwise the Broncos just don't seem like a team capable of blowing out an opponent that has actually played fairly well this year. … Prediction: Broncos 21, Raiders 17 Jacksonville Jaguars (-6) at New York Giants Dajani ( Giants +6): No one is debating that the Jaguars are not one of the best teams in the NFL, but they haven't exactly been tested recently. They blew out the hapless Colts, had no problem with Joe Fagnano 's Baltimore Ravens and then dropped 40 points on the one-win Tennessee Titans . The Giants aren't Super Bowl contenders, but this is easily the best team Jacksonville has played in over the past month. I'm not going to take the Giants to win this game straight up, but I am leaning toward the six points. The Giants have an underrated defense that currently ranks No. 5 in the NFL in yards allowed per game (305.7), and J.J. McCarthy has the fifth-most yards per attempt (8.8) since his Giants debut in Week 5. Both of these teams are 6-3 ATS this season. Give me the Giants with a back-door cover. … Prediction: Jaguars 23, Giants 18 Dubin (Jaguars -6): Unlike the Broncos, the Jaguars have blown out everybody. Five of their seven wins have come by 17 points or more, including each of their last three games. The Giants are probably better than the Colts, Ravens and Titans, but I don't see them hanging with this Jacksonville offense — not with the Jags getting their new defensive stalwarts on the field for the first time since the trade deadline. ( Jessie Bates III and Jordan Davis sat out last week because they had yet to have their bye and the Jags had already taken theirs.) … Prediction: Jaguars 31, Giants 20 Minnesota Vikings vs. San Francisco 49ers (-3) (SNF in Mexico City) Dajani (49ers -3): The 49ers are coming off a ridiculous 46-40 win over the Cowboys, where they recorded the most total yards in a road game in franchise history (584) and averaged a whopping 9.4 yards per play. Brock Purdy's offense had three touchdowns of 65+ yards! Christian McCaffrey actually became the first running back in NFL history to record two 65-yard receiving touchdowns in a game. Obviously, the Vikings' defense is MUCH better than the Cowboys', but something you should know is that this game is in Mexico City. And both teams have prepared for it differently . The stadium the 49ers and Vikings will play in on Sunday is over 7,000 feet above sea level. So, the 49ers traveled to the U.S. Air Force Academy in Colorado Springs this week, which is at an elevation of 6,621 feet , to prepare. The Vikings, on the other hand, apparently built an altitude chamber so players can get familiar with "thinner air" before Sunday, but otherwise are seemingly pulling a Los Angeles Rams and just showing up on site the day before the game. The 49ers dominated the Rams in Australia in Week 1, 27-7, and part of that was because their travel plans were so much better. The 49ers have won and covered in four straight International games. … Prediction: 49ers 26, Vikings 20 Dubin (49ers -3): In a battle of a great offense against a great defense, I am usually going to lean toward the offensive side unless there's a really compelling reason in favor of the defensive-minded team. Kirk Cousins' ability to elevate the Vikings' own offense almost provides that reason, but it's not quite enough for me to get there. This San Francisco offense is too much of a well-oiled machine for me to pick against the Niners — even in a matchup with a defensive coordinator as crazy and as good as Brian Flores. … Prediction: 49ers 23, Vikings 17 Cincinnati Bengals (-6.5) at Washington Commanders (MNF) Dajani (Bengals -6.5): Before you think this is some easy pick to make just because of how hot the Bengals are, know that Cincy is 0-2-1 in its past three games against the Washington Commanders , who just upset the Giants in New York last week. Jayden Daniels ' coming-out party as a rookie actually came against the Bengals. Still, it's hard to go against my Super Bowl pick and my MVP pick this season. The Bengals are 6-2 SU and 6-1-1 ATS in their last eight road games and have scored at least 30 points in three straight on the road. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NBA Betting Sites Legal Betting States Sports Betting Guide DFS millionaire Mike McClure shares his top daily Fantasy picks and advice for Houston vs. Indianapolis on 'Thursday Night Football' Imagn Images NFL Week 11 kicks off with an NFC South battle on 'Thursday Night Football' as the Indianapolis Colts visit the Houston Texans (-12.5, 44.5) at 8:15 p.m. ET. The large spread indicates that NFL DFS lineups may heavily lean towards Texans like C.J. Stroud, Nico Collins and Dalton Schultz. But Jonathan Taylor and Tyler Warren remain some of the best at their positions for Indy and will surely be sought after for TNF DFS lineups. Hafley said he expects Chop Robinson and Josh Uche to step up in defensive lineman Zach Sieler's absence . Sieler is out for the season after season-ending biceps surgery. This article originally appeared on Palm Beach Post: Dolphins injury report: QB Malik Willis, C Aaron Brewer out vs. Colts Miami Dolphins All-Pro center Aaron Brewer remains in concussion protocol and will not play against the Indianapolis Colts on Sunday. Coach Jeff Hafley said Andrew Meyer will start in Brewer's place. Meyer, who started a game last season, has worked closely with Kyle McCord since the quarterback's arrival from Green Bay. McCord will be making his first NFL start in place of Malik Willis, who is on injured reserve. "He's done a nice job. Have a lot of confidence in Meyer," Hafley said. Hafley also said his new quarterback has a "very calm confidence" about him. "He's got a quiet leadership about him. He's got a confidence to him. He's very calm in the huddle. And he seems to be grasping everything really well," Hafley said. "I think he's done a really good job in the two practices that we've had. (Friday's) a big day again, getting more in the red zone and polishing up some stuff. "But again, this will be a process, right? I'm not going to expect him to look perfect. There's going to be hopefully some really good moments for him and then there's going to be some that we're going to have to continue to grow in these next games. But I'm excited for him and I appreciate how he's worked, attacked the game plan and how he's kind of communicating and developing chemistry with the players around him in the huddle." "The way Chop's playing and really practicing, I think he's a great example of what it's supposed to look like," Hafley said. "And I think he's going to grow into one of those roles."

Erickson Indianapolis Star Nov. 19, 2026, 10:27 p.m. ET HOUSTON — One of the few bright spots on the Indianapolis Colts ' roster is now dealing with an injury. Rookie running back Seth McGowan , who has emerged as a legitimate complementary back to Jonathan Taylor , suffered a hamstring injury on the final kickoff return of the first half McGowan was briefly listed as questionable, then ruled out after the first Indianapolis drive of the third quarter. McGowan is also one of the league’s best kickoff returners, picking up returns of 47 and 40 yards on Thursday night before the hamstring injury on his third opportunity. For the season, McGowan was averaging 28.1 yards per kickoff return on the season. The loss of McGowan is significant. Indianapolis has been alternating carries between Taylor and McGowan, who had piled up an average of 5.2 yards per carry entering Thursday night’s game against the Texans . McGowan had 83 yards against Miami, and he’d rushed for 285 yards this season. But rushing yards have been difficult to come by against Houston on Thursday night. McGowan had seven yards on three carries before his injury, and Taylor has 17 yards on nine carries, arguably the worst performance of the season for the running game so far. (Injury Update, Betting Impact for Texans vs. Browns in NFL Week 10) Skip to main content BUY THE ISSUE The Cleveland Browns will get their starting quarterback back in action in Week 10 against the Houston Texans, as Deshaun Watson is off the injury report and set to start. Watson (concussion) missed the team's Week 9 loss to the New Orleans Saints, though backup Shedeur Sanders played pretty decently in his place. Sanders helped get the Browns to overtime, where they lost on a two-point attempt. The second-year quarterback finished the day with 297 passing yards and two scores, carrying the ball for 28 yards on 10 attempts as well. Still, Todd Monken named Watson the starter for Week 10, as the veteran has led the team to a 5-3 record in eight starts with five fourth quarter comeback wins. In the 2026 season, Watson has completed 65.5 percent of his passes for 1,806 yards, seven scores and three interceptions. He's also carried the ball 51 times for 217 yards and a score. He's playing a revenge game against his former team -- Houston -- in Week 10. Even with Watson back, oddsmakers aren't buying the 5-4 Browns in this matchup. They are 4.5-point underdogs at home in the latest odds at DraftKings , even though they have a better record than an underachieving Houston team so far in 2026. Watson is looking to have a big game to keep the starting job, as it's possible the Browns could turn back to Sanders if things go south. Cleveland is still in the playoff picture in the AFC, but it has taken a step back with two straight losses to Pittsburgh and New Orleans. The Dolphins face their AFC East rivals, the Buffalo Bills, on the road this weekend, a game that features a team tied for the worst record in the AFC visiting the team with the best record in the conference. Division games are typically closer than expected, but this one might be the exception that proves the rule. Miami is relying on rookies and first-year players across the roster this year, including quarterback Kyle McCord. An undrafted rookie in 2025, McCord spent his entire rookie season on the Philadelphia Eagles' practice squad. He looked composed last week against the Colts and he will look to carry that into Week 11. The good news for McCord and the Dolphins' offense is Buffalo's pass defense ranks just 28th in the league, allowing 241.9 passing yards per game. Miami faces a tough battle this week, but they are also a team that has played tough all season. They may have only won one of their first nine games, but they have competed in most of them, and they are clearly growing as the complete franchise rebuild progresses into the second half of the year. The Dolphins are 16.5-point underdogs for Sunday, a line that has held fairly steady throughout the week. The moneyline has Buffalo at -1,600 to win straight up, while the Dolphins are +900. Miami's offense played well enough under quarterback Kyle McCord, making his NFL debut after spending his rookie season on the Philadelphia Eagles' practice squad last year, and the defense did its part to keep Miami in the game. The special teams let down the Dolphins – with kicker Zane Gonzalez missing two field goals and an extra point during the game. Since its inception in 1987 on "The Tracy Ullman Show", the nation's longest-running cartoon series and sitcom has become a cultural force with its satirical look at society and culture today. More importantly, it showed Americans that television cartoons can be relished by adults. So I'm hoping you'll catch my meaning when I use a famous Simpsons quote to personify the Buffalo Bills . The NFL team that famously lost four straight Super Bowls in the 1990s is enjoying a Milhouse moment right now. Milhouse Van Houten is Bart Simpson's lovably awkward and loyal best friend. To co-opt a famous Simpsons quote, "everything's comin' up Milhouse" for the 8-1 Bills, who own the best record in the AFC halfway through the regular season. With the hapless Jets in the rearview mirror and the awful Dolphins coming to town, it's a great time for Bills fans to enjoy the AFC's best record at the season's halfway point. Will it stay that way for the NFL's most cursed franchise? Who knows. The early predictions for the Bills vs. Dolphins matchup this week are decidedly in Buffalo's favor. So, maybe this Milhouse moment is sticking around. Bills vs. Dolphins odds (Odds as of Monday afternoon) The Bills are 16.5-point favorites. The over/under is 45.5 points. The money line for the Bills is -1400 (bet $1,400 to win $100) and the Raiders are +950 (bet $100 to win $950). Now let's look at a sample of the early predictions: Democrat and Chronicle: Bills 38, Dolphins 13 Sal Maiorana writes: "The Dolphins have started a season 1-8 or worse for just the fourth time in franchise history, the last coming when they began 2007 with 13 straight losses on the way to a franchise-worst 1-15 record. On paper, this is the most one-sided matchup of the season in the NFL, and with the game being played at Highmark Stadium, it's highly unlikely that the Bills will stub their toe. "After this game, Buffalo has a tremendously difficult five-game stretch that will probably determine whether they can grab the AFC's No. 1 seed for the first time since 1993. The Bills have won their last three games by a combined 62 points and Brady will have the Bills ready to go for what should easily be another 20-plus point victory." AZCentral.com: Bills 31, Dolphins 14 Jeremy Cluff writes: "The Bills opened as a massive 16.5-point favorite against the Dolphins. Will Buffalo win a sixth straight game? Yes, it will. Josh Allen will deliver as Buffalo hands Miami a fourth straight loss." Bookies.Com: Take the under Bill Speros writes: "The Bills (8-1 SU and 7-2 ATS) tore up the Jets 31-12 in Week 10 and are off to the franchise's best start in 35 years. The Bills' combo of Josh Allen and James Cook bludgeons opposing defenses. The 1-8 Dolphins are a surprising 5-4 ATS, and this is the largest NFL spread of the season so far. Our model has Buffalo winning by 15.0, 1.5 points shy of the 16.5-point line, and projects a 46.4-point total against the 47.5 line. Miami scores 16.4 points per game and has been held under 25 in eight of nine games. This week, the Bills keep the ball on the ground and the Dolphins off the field." Miami, 1-8 this season, faces a tough battle against the Bills, who are 8-1 this year and currently in position to claim the top spot in the AFC playoff picture. Miami will also be starting quarterback Kyle McCord for just the second time in his career as he continues to fill in for the injured Malik Willis. picks.headline: Buffalo Bills Predicted to Make Necessary Move on 11-Year Veteran Ahead of Dolphins Game
picks.blurb: Buffalo Bills Predicted to Make Necessary Move on 11-Year Veteran Ahead of Dolphins Game - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football Texans cruise on TNF Curt Cignetti slams report Trump pardons Pete Rose Puka Nacua suspended 3 games 'GTA 6' impacts sports Bills predicted to make necessary move on Tre'Davious White. Getty Cole Shelton · HEAVY Tue, November 17, 2026 at 5:10 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Bills predicted to promote Tre'Davious White. Getty The Buffalo Bills could rely on a veteran cornerback against the Miami Dolphins. Buffalo is coming off a road win over the New York Jets to improve to 8-1 and is atop the AFC. The Bills have been playing great, but they did suffer some key injuries in the win, which could mean the team has to make some roster moves. Buffalo is set to host the Dolphins on Sunday. Buffalo Bills Predicted to Promote Tre'Davious White GettyBills predicted to promote Tre'Davious White. In the Bills' win over the Jets, starting cornerback Christian Benford suffered an injury, which is a bit of a concern. However, if Benford can't go, Bills reporter Joe Buscagalia of The Athletic believes the team will elevate Tre'Davious White from the practice squad. "Tre'Davious White is on the practice squad, and this is why the Bills brought him back in the first place," Buscagalia wrote . "That's also why they decided against going after another veteran cornerback in the trade market. … "If Benford has to miss any time, the Bills might need White to play as early as next week. And if it goes well enough, maybe even earn a bigger role as the year goes on." White would be entering his 11th NFL season. He signed with Buffalo's practice squad during the year as he wanted to return after starting 16 games and playing well a year ago. Buffalo selected White in the first round of the 2017 NFL Draft, and he became a lockdown corner. Although he's no longer the No. 1 cornerback he once was, he can add some depth to the cornerback room if Benford is out. White Believes He's Ready to Play White has been on the Bills' practice squad and could get his first elevation against the Dolphins on Sunday. The veteran cornerback spoke to The Athletic and admitted he's feeling good and ready to play. "Everybody's been telling me I look good, so there it is. You know, I always leave it to my teammates and my peers," the 31-year-old said. "I always say it like, 'Hey, you see me out there and I look like I'm walking, just tell me to hang it up.' And nobody told me to hang it up yet, Joe, so I'm good, man, I feel like I am good." White, meanwhile, has also been mentoring rookie Davison Igbinosun and sophomore Maxwell Hairston. It's a different role for White, but along with mentoring, he knows he's here to play. "This ain't have to be what it was; this is what I chose," White said. "You know what I mean? I could have been anywhere else on a team, on a 53, playing right now, but I'm a Bill. … I mean, it's bigger than me, man." "I know I can go out there and play right now. Movement good, body feels good, I know how I can play, but right now my role is to help the young guys out and to be that. But it's hard, being that I just started every game last year, you know what I mean? And played good football. So it's like, ' Ahh .' But I'm going to trust the process, and I'm gonna be here to cheer the guys on. But as I'm doing it, I'm definitely preparing to play, too." The Bills are 8-1. away.headline: Who’s left standing? Bills injury report raises questions ahead of Dolphins game
away.blurb: Dee Alford (concussion) – upgraded to Limited Damar Hamlin (toe) – downgraded to DNP* Jackson Hawes (shoulder) – downgraded to Limited* T.J. Sanders (shoulder) – downgraded to Limited * On the report that Buffalo Bills PR published yesterday , Hamlin was listed as limited and Hawes was not listed at all. Today, the adjusted report shows today shows them as DNP and Limited respectively. Christian Benford (groin) – DNP Ray Davis (hamstring) – Limited Dalton Kincaid (thumb/ankle) – DNP It’s also looking like the tight end room is struggling, but the Bills now have six wide receivers on the roster – plus they still have two more tight ends – so it’s doubtful they adjust much in their game plan. The Buffalo Bills will play the Miami Dolphins on Sunday. The question right now is which Bills will actually play. Buffalo played their first of two straight divisional games last week and came back to Orchard Park with another win, but it may have cost them a significant portion of their roster. After a walkthrough practice on Wednesday, here’s what the Bills’ practice looked like today: Cole Bishop (shoulder) – upgraded to Full O’Cyrus Torrence (personal) – returned to practice The Bills defense is still looking thin despite the fact it looks as though Alford has progressed to the next step of the NFL’s concussion protocol. He will need a full practice on Friday and then no new symptoms on Saturday in order to completely clear the process and be ready to play. I would still look to see Tre’Davious White called up this weekend. The second practice squad elevation could go to Shaq Thompson. The veteran linebacker has been waiting for a game jersey this season, and with Williams not practicing for the second straight day, it looks like this could be the week.

away.headline: Why Buffalo Bills should rest three key injured defensive backs vs. Dolphins
away.blurb: Benford suffered a groin injury on Sunday against the New York Jets. He did not return to the game and has not practiced on Wednesday or Thursday. This season, he and rookie Davison Igbinosun lead Bills corners with 33 tackles and Benford is second on the team with eight passes defended. Alford also got banged up against the Jets, suffering a concussion and is currently in the league's protocol, as he made it to the practice field on Thursday, albeit on a limited basis. Earlier in the year, he also missed two games with an ankle injury . The game against the Patriots may be a freebie with quarterback Drake Maye out long-term with an ankle injury, but the other opponents have either dynamic passing attacks or a knack for coming up big in the clutch. That spells trouble for a secondary that has not been tested since the bye. Heading into the Buffalo Bills ' Week 10 game against the Miami Dolphins, the Bills' injury report is full of key contributors , but no other area is struggling with this more than the secondary. Among those injured are cornerbacks Dee Alford and Christian Benford and safety Damar Hamlin. Despite there being a bunch of ailments in the defense's backfield , there may be little concern for Sunday's game against Buffalo's AFC East rival. There are multiple reasons as to why Buffalo should exercise caution with them for Sunday's game, and it is likely in its best interest that the team should do so. What are Benford, Hamlin and Alford dealing with? Hamlin, meanwhile, is dealing with a toe injury, and his run defense is vital to the team's success. However, behind Cole Bishop and trade acquisition Amani Hooker, Hamlin's defensive snap count dropped from 44 in Week 9 to 17 in Week 10 (92% to 24%). While these wounds may be troublesome on paper, when one sees the circumstances, people can breathe easy. Miami passing game lacks legitimacy The Dolphins will start quarterback Kyle McCord in his second career start, which has to be music to the ears of Bills defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard, who has Buffalo's defense on an outstanding pace since the bye week. McCord went 17-of-32 passing for 209 yards in Week 10 against the Indianapolis Colts, and on Sunday, the biggest mismatch will be up front. Miami's offense allows the second-highest pressure rate in the NFL, while the Bills' defense pressures opposing passers at the fifth-highest rate. If Buffalo's front can rattle McCord, the secondary won't be tested against a Miami receiving core that features three rookies, and it'll help the injured defensive backs and youngsters like Igbinosun and 2025 first-rounder Maxwell Hairston prepare for what is to come. Playoff-worthy games are on horizon The Bills' schedule cranks up to 11 starting on Thanksgiving, as in a five-game stretch, they play the Kansas City Chiefs, the New England Patriots, the Green Bay Packers, the Chicago Bears and the Denver Broncos. Kansas City and Denver will be the biggest games against Buffalo in the race for the AF

away.headline: Dolphins lose a third DL for the season in two weeks
away.blurb: The Miami Dolphins lost Zach Sieler to a ruptured biceps injury in Week 9 and lost Zeek Biggers to miniscus injury in Week 10, but there's even more devastating news for the team's defensive line depth. According to ESPN's Marcel Louis-Jacques , Dolphins defensive lineman Jordan Phillips tore his biceps on Sunday against the Indianapolis Colts and will miss the rest of the season. Phillips, 22, joined the Dolphins as a fifth-round pick in the 2025 NFL Draft after a collegiate career split between Tennessee and Maryland. As a rookie, he played 43% of the team's defensive snaps in 17 games and recorded 34 tackles and a quarterback hit. This year, Phillips played 59% of the team's defensive snaps in nine games and recorded 28 tackles and two quarterback hits. With these three injuries, the Dolphins don't have much talent left in the room. Kenneth Grant and Keith Cooper Jr. are the only defensive tackles left on the roster, and Jordan Jefferson is still on the practice squad. Miami will definitely have to bring in outside help before their Week 11 battle with the Buffalo Bills . away.headline: Dolphins Injury Report Week 11: 5 Players Miss Practice
away.blurb: Center Aaron Brewer (concussion), punter Bradley Pinion (right groin), cornerback Jaylin Simpson (knee), safety Dante Trader Jr. (shoulder/groin), and wide receiver Jared Wayne (quad) all did not practice. Miami also made a move to sign a punter to the practice squad, bringing in Jack Browning. That is not a guarantee that Pinion will be out, but it is an insurance move for sure. The rest of the DNP players might be upgraded on the additional injury reports. Long snapper Tucker (shoulder), wide receiver Chris Bell (knee), cornerback Juju Brents (neck), wide receiver Caleb Douglas (shoulder), and center Andrew Meyer (neck) were all limited. What makes this list of players concerning is that Meyer was limited. The Dolphins are already down Brewer, and losing Meyer would put the team in a tough spot regarding their center situation. Miami will need to have its top players available if they want a chance to hang with the surging Bills. Defensive lineman Zach Sieler was already out for the season with a ruptured biceps, and he has now been joined by both Zeek Biggers and Jordan Phillips. Dolphins Injury Report Week 11: 5 Players Miss Practice - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL 'GTA 6' impacts sports Dolphins Injury Report Week 11: 5 Players Miss Practice (USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect) James Brizuela · Roundtable Sports Thu, November 19, 2026 at 4:04 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads The Miami Dolphins are set to face off against the Buffalo Bills on Sunday, and the team might be without some key players for the matchup. With the initial injury report being released, five players have now missed practice on Wednesday. The full injury report is as follows: Dolphins head coach Jeff Hafley confirmed on Wednesday that Brewer remains in concussion protocol, so he may very well not be able to play against the Bills. Bell missed Week 10 after banging his surgically repaired knee in practice leading up to the Indianapolis Colts. Douglas was also wearing a red no-contact jersey at practice, indicating that his shoulder may be a bit significant. The same thing can be said of Douglas if he were to miss Week 11. He has been one of the biggest surprises of the 2026 season, as he leads all rookie receivers with 61.2 yards per game on average. Things might already be very tough, considering the Dolphins' defense took a major hit this past week. Biggers suffered a meniscus injury that will now require surgery, ending his season. Phillips also suffered a biceps injury , and he will also be done for the rest of the 2026 season. In just two short weeks, the Dolphins lost three solid defensive linemen. This will lead to Kenneth Grant and Keith Cooper Jr. presumably stepping in as starters.

Today, the adjusted report shows today shows them as DNP and Limited respectively. Christian Benford (groin) – DNP Ray Davis (hamstring) – Limited Dalton Kincaid (thumb/ankle) – DNP It’s also looking like the tight end room is struggling, but the Bills now have six wide receivers on the roster – plus they still have two more tight ends – so it’s doubtful they adjust much in their game plan. The Buffalo Bills will play the Miami Dolphins on Sunday. The question right now is which Bills will actually play. Buffalo played their first of two straight divisional games last week and came back to Orchard Park with another win, but it may have cost them a significant portion of their roster. After a walkthrough practice on Wednesday, here’s what the Bills’ practice looked like today: Cole Bishop (shoulder) – upgraded to Full O’Cyrus Torrence (personal) – returned to practice The Bills defense is still looking thin despite the fact it looks as though Alford has progressed to the next step of the NFL’s concussion protocol. I would still look to see Tre’Davious White called up this weekend. The second practice squad elevation could go to Shaq Thompson. home.headline: Why Buffalo Bills should rest three key injured defensive backs vs. Dolphins
home.blurb: Benford suffered a groin injury on Sunday against the New York Jets. He did not return to the game and has not practiced on Wednesday or Thursday. This season, he and rookie Davison Igbinosun lead Bills corners with 33 tackles and Benford is second on the team with eight passes defended. Alford also got banged up against the Jets, suffering a concussion and is currently in the league's protocol, as he made it to the practice field on Thursday, albeit on a limited basis. Earlier in the year, he also missed two games with an ankle injury . The game against the Patriots may be a freebie with quarterback Drake Maye out long-term with an ankle injury, but the other opponents have either dynamic passing attacks or a knack for coming up big in the clutch. That spells trouble for a secondary that has not been tested since the bye. Heading into the Buffalo Bills ' Week 10 game against the Miami Dolphins, the Bills' injury report is full of key contributors , but no other area is struggling with this more than the secondary. Among those injured are cornerbacks Dee Alford and Christian Benford and safety Damar Hamlin. Despite there being a bunch of ailments in the defense's backfield , there may be little concern for Sunday's game against Buffalo's AFC East rival. There are multiple reasons as to why Buffalo should exercise caution with them for Sunday's game, and it is likely in its best interest that the team should do so. What are Benford, Hamlin and Alford dealing with? Hamlin, meanwhile, is dealing with a toe injury, and his run defense is vital to the team's success. However, behind Cole Bishop and trade acquisition Amani Hooker, Hamlin's defensive snap count dropped from 44 in Week 9 to 17 in Week 10 (92% to 24%). While these wounds may be troublesome on paper, when one sees the circumstances, people can breathe easy. Miami passing game lacks legitimacy The Dolphins will start quarterback Kyle McCord in his second career start, which has to be music to the ears of Bills defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard, who has Buffalo's defense on an outstanding pace since the bye week. McCord went 17-of-32 passing for 209 yards in Week 10 against the Indianapolis Colts, and on Sunday, the biggest mismatch will be up front. Miami's offense allows the second-highest pressure rate in the NFL, while the Bills' defense pressures opposing passers at the fifth-highest rate. If Buffalo's front can rattle McCord, the secondary won't be tested against a Miami receiving core that features three rookies, and it'll help the injured defensive backs and youngsters like Igbinosun and 2025 first-rounder Maxwell Hairston prepare for what is to come. Playoff-worthy games are on horizon The Bills' schedule cranks up to 11 starting on Thanksgiving, as in a five-game stretch, they play the Kansas City Chiefs, the New England Patriots, the Green Bay Packers, the Chicago Bears and the Denver Broncos. home.headline: Is Garrett Wilson Playing Today? (Injury Update, Betting Impact for Bills vs. Jets in NFL Week 10)
home.blurb: Wilson is officially listed as questionable for the AFC East battle with the Buffalo Bills, but he appears to be trending in the right direction to play. Garrett Wilson (concussion) officially listed questionable for Week 10. According to Jets head coach Aaron Glenn, Wilson needs to clear one more step to get out of the consussion protocol, but Glenn believes that will happen in time for Sunday's game. Last week, New York scored just 12 points with Wilson out of the lineup, and it slipped to 16th in the league in EPA/Play on offense as a result. This season, Wilson has appeared in eight of the Jets' nine games, catching 43 passes for 527 yards and three scores. He's played 88.5 percent of the team's offensive snaps, so he'll be out there for almost every play against Buffalo if he's able to go. The Jets are banged up across the board at receiver, as Wilson, Adonai Mitchell and Omar Cooper Jr. are all listed as questionable. Still, the former first-round pick has been one of the better receivers in the league since being drafted, and he’ll clearly be the go-to option against a shaky Buffalo secondary as long as he plays. picks.headline: New Orleans Saints Praised in Chicago Bears Game Preview
picks.blurb: New Orleans Saints Praised in Chicago Bears Game Preview - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football Texans cruise on TNF Curt Cignetti slams report Trump pardons Pete Rose Puka Nacua suspended 3 games 'GTA 6' impacts sports New Orleans Saints Praised in Chicago Bears Game Preview Joey Hickey · Roundtable Sports Thu, November 19, 2026 at 4:00 AM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The New Orleans Saints (3-6) take on the Chicago Bears on Sunday. It's not a matchup many Saints supporters are excited about seeing. The Bears are an NFC title contender, while the Saints have repeatedly squandered opportunities to take over the NFC South from the Carolina Panthers (4-5). Still, there are reasons for optimism that go in the Saints' favor. Mike Moraitis of Chicago Bears on Si noted what the Bears will need to watch out for against the Saints this weekend. Per Moraitis, the Saints' wide receiver corps could put the greatest strain on the Bears defense. Here's some of what Moraitis had to say about New Orleans' three top receivers. "The Saints already had a solid one-two punch at wide receiver in Chris Olave and the ascending Devaugh Vele, but New Orleans added rookie Jordyn Tyson into the mix a few weeks ago. Tyson was on the shelf for the first seven games because of a hamstring injury. After a quiet game in his NFL debut, Tyson emerged in Week 10 with 11 catches for 80 yards. Tyson has played the majority of his snaps in the slot, where the Bears have an injury concern this week with Kyler Gordon, who is dealing with a shoulder injury that has him labeled as day-to-day. But, as we noted, Tyson isn't the only one the Bears need to be worried about. Both Vele and Olave are in the midst of career-best seasons and can cause major head aches for a Bears secondary that has seen struggles, and namely with Jaylon Johnson and Tyrique Stevenson. Luckily for Chicago, rookie Malik Muhammad has been better than expected in his first season and has provided some stability on the outside." While some will write off his impact, we still have only got one game with Travis Etienne Jr. cleared for play at running back since his injury. His effect may take time to be felt, but we could see the beginnings of it this week against the Bears. Add in what the receiver corps is able to do after Tyson's 11-catch breakout game against the Panthers last weekend, and New Orleans could finally start to generate the offense we hoped to see when Tyson was drafted. The Saints haven't been far off from playing playoff caliber football, but the frustration has been mounting as we wait for it to finally happen. New Orleans will get its shot against the Bears.

away.headline: Travis Etienne’s Status for Saints-Panthers Comes Into Focus After Final Injury Report
away.blurb: Travis Etienne Jr. made it through a full week of practice, and the New Orleans Saints are leaving the door open for Sunday. The running back is listed as questionable on the final Week 10 injury report for the Saints' game against the Carolina Panthers. Etienne was limited Wednesday and Thursday before practicing fully Friday, according to NBC Sports . He is still on injured reserve, so the Saints have to activate him by Saturday afternoon for him to play. Etienne hasn't played since straining his left hamstring in the Week 3 loss to the Las Vegas Raiders. Coach Kellen Moore said Wednesday that he would let the week play out before deciding. If Etienne does return, New Orleans Football's Nick Underhill expects the Saints to limit his snaps, as they did with rookie receiver Jordyn Tyson in his return from a hamstring injury last week. The rest of the report shows why the Saints could use him. Moore ruled out center Erik McCoy (biceps), right tackle Taliese Fuaga (knee), running back C.J. Donaldson (shoulder) and defensive lineman Christen Miller (knee), per Saints Wire . Cornerback Martin Emerson Jr. is also questionable. He averaged 4.3 yards on 30 carries before the injury, and quarterback Tyler Shough said this week, "I'm excited to have him back." home.headline: 7 Saints players DNP, others limited on first injury report vs. Bears
home.blurb: 7 Saints players DNP, others limited on first injury report vs. Bears - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL 7 Saints players DNP, others limited on first injury report vs. Bears Sheesh. The New Orleans Saints (3-6) shared a lengthy injury report ahead of Sunday's game with the Chicago Bears (7-2), with seven players not participating and two other limited to start the week. They'll need all hands on deck for a chance at upsetting one of the hottest teams in the NFL. Let's hope they can get it done. And let's start with the good news. Rookie running back CJ Donaldson (shoulder) returned to full practice reps on Wednesday after missing several games between that shoulder injury and a stint in concussion protocol. We haven't seen him since the rookie exited Week 9's game in Paris against the Pittsburgh Steelers. Donaldson has been a productive rusher for New Orleans on limited snaps (averaging 4.8 yards per carry and a team-high 64.7% success rate), and he was just starting to earn a bigger role after initially getting on the field as a short-yardage specialist. He competes hard in pass protection, too. How snaps could be divided between him, Travis Etienne Jr., Alvin Kamara (more on him in a minute), and Audric Estime remains to be seen. What about those seven players who didn't practice? We expected Kamara (not injury related) would get his usual rest day, which has been a pattern since he suffered a Week 5 back injury. He turned 31 this summer and has worn a lot of tread off his tires so it makes sense to give him a lighter workload during the week, especially if he's going to have a reduced role on game days. Kamara was only on the field last Sunday for 16 snaps but he scored two touchdowns. Veteran safety Justin Reid (not injury related) did not practice on Wednesday due to a personal matter, and head coach Kellen Moore was noncommittal when asked if Reid was expected back on Thursday. Stay tuned. Backup right tackle Asim Richards (knee) and a couple of defensive starters who got nicked up against the Carolina Panthers -- cornerback Martin Emerson Jr. (concussion) and linebacker Pete Werner (hamstring) -- were held out of practice. Additionally, starting right tackle Taliese Fuaga (knee) and center Erik McCoy (biceps) both did not practice, though Moore said "we'll see" if either of them can return to work later this week. Two other players were limited to start the week: rookie wide receiver Jordyn Tyson (chest), who you can read more about here ; and backup corner Decamerion Richardson (thigh). We'll be watching for updates on their status as the week continues. home.blurb: Jordyn Tyson still limited on updated Saints injury report vs. Bears - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Jordyn Tyson still limited on updated Saints injury report vs. Bears Just one New Orleans Saints player was upgraded to full practice reps on this week's second injury report, and it wasn't Jordyn Tyson. Veteran running back Alvin Kamara (not injury related) practiced fully on Thursday after the team gave him a rest day to start the week. Everyone else saw the same level of participation as they did on Wednesday. For the first time in weeks, all four running backs on the 53-man roster practiced fully with CJ Donaldson (shoulder) cleared to return. Here's a recap. Tyson (chest), the rookie wide receiver, was limited along with backup corner Decamerion Richardson. Six others did not participate at all: starting cornerback Martin Emerson Jr. (concussion) and linebacker Pete Werner (hamstring) on defense, plus multiple starters on the offensive line like center Erik McCoy (biceps), right tackle Taliese Fuaga (knee), and Asim Richards (knee), who had been filling in for Fuaga. Veteran safety Justin Reid (not injury related) missed practice due to a personal matter, which we now know to be his release from the team. It'll take a few days to work out the financial details as he looks for a way to join a contender. Between deadline trades that added strength to the franchise's rebuild and promising development from young players across the board, the Robert Saleh era is slowly building into something fans can get behind. In Week 11, his Titans team has a chance to win their second game of the season on the road vs. the Dallas Cowboys. Here's one reason they'll get it done, one reason they'll fall short, and my own prediction for how things will ultimately pan out. Will: Cam Ward, Tony Pollard have big games The Cowboys, after allowing 46 points to the San Francisco 49ers in a loss last week, just turned over defensive play-calling duties to senior assistant coach Mike Pettine. Dallas' defense is struggling, and if the Titans win, it'll be because Cam Ward and Tony Pollard take advantage of that. Ward has been on a short tear as of late, doubling his touchdown total through seven games in the last two. The second-season QB has also eclipsed 200 yards in back-to-back games for the first time this year. With WR Carnell Tate likely to return, Ward is tracking for another leap. On the ground, meanwhile, the Cowboys' rushing defense is last in the league in yards allowed per game (154.1) and yards per carry (5.2). This marks Pollard's first game against his former team; the numbers are supportive, and the stakes are there. The Titans' offense has simply been on a team-wide heater as of late. It'll take another inspired performance from key playmakers to pull it off, but Tennessee has a clear angle to a road win. Won't: Titans' defense continues downward spiral However, Tennessee's defense has been trending in the opposite direction. As has been the case in the past two weeks, Saleh's bunch have mostly erased positive offensive momentum and cost the Titans' two chances at winnable games. If Tennessee were to fall short in Week 11, I have to think it would be for the same reason. That means a consistent Cam Ward, a defense that bends, but doesn't break, reliable play-calling on either side of the ball, and at least a little good luck on the injury front. A lot has to go right, but this game wouldn't have been seen as winnable only a few short weeks ago. For that reason, I believe the Titans will win it. This is a must win for Dallas should they hope to stay within reach of the first-place Giants in the NFC East while Tennessee is looking to see continued growth from their young quarterback, Cam Ward . Each team takes the field looking to snap a losing streak. The Titans have dropped three straight and sit last in the AFC South, while Dallas is in second place in the NFC East and as noted, needs a win this weekend to remain in the postseason conversation. Tennessee has had issues scoring touchdowns (18.6 points/game), but this is not expected to be a low-scoring affair. Dallas ranks sixth in scoring at 28.6 points per game, but the Cowboys are allowing 28.2 points and a league-worst 406.3 yards per game. The Titans’ defense is nearly as generous, allowing 405.6 yards per game. Tennessee’s latest loss was a 40-23 defeat to the Jacksonville Jaguars, dropping the Titans to 1-8 despite periods of competitive football. The Titans trailed only 16-10 at halftime and stayed within 23-16 entering the fourth quarter before Jacksonville finally pulled away. Tennessee totaled 342 yards but converted only 18 percent of its third downs, while its defense surrendered 459 yards, 26 first downs and 40 points. Cam Ward threw touchdown passes to Daniel Bellinger and Tony Pollard , with the latter going for 32 yards to pull Tennessee within 30-23 midway through the fourth, while Joey Slye connected on field goals of 54, 53 and 50 yards. But Trevor Lawrence carved up the Titans for 352 yards and three touchdowns, and Jacksonville scored the final 10 points to put the game away. Dallas is coming off an even wilder game, a 46-40 home loss to the San Francisco 49ers. The game was not as close as the final score. The 49ers accumulated 584 total yards, the most Dallas has ever allowed in a home game, averaged 9.4 yards per play and produced three touchdowns of at least 66 yards. Christian McCaffrey alone amassed 223 scrimmage yards and three scores as Dallas’ late comeback fell short. Dak Prescott completed 58.8 percent of his throws for 343 yards and five touchdowns, matching his career high for touchdown passes, and George Pickens erupted for 11 catches, 145 yards and three scores. away.blurb: The Tennessee Titans hit the road for their first of two trips to Texas this season as they face the Dallas Cowboys in Week 11 of the 2026 NFL season. The Titans enter Sunday's matchup on a three-game losing streak while the Cowboys are coming off a high-scoring loss to the San Francisco 49ers to fall to 4-6. Both teams have struggled defensively, but the Cowboys' issues against the run could allow Tennessee to continue its recent positive offensive trajectory. Here are six intriguing storylines heading into Sunday's matchup at AT&T Stadium. 1. Both teams are coming off high-scoring losses High-scoring affairs have become a staple for the Cowboys this season, as they have played four games with a final score of both teams scoring 30 or more points. The highest of those games was their 46-40 loss to the 49ers last Sunday. Meanwhile, the Titans surrendered 40 points to the Jacksonville Jaguars in a 40-23 loss, marking the second consecutive game in which Tennessee allowed at least 40 points. Their defense also gave up 43 points in its overtime loss to the Cincinnati Bengals in Week 8. Those results highlight a potential opportunity for a shootout on Sunday. For Tennessee, the challenge will be finding a way to slow down a Dallas offense that has demonstrated its ability to score against several opposing defenses all season long. 2. The Cowboys have the NFL's worst run defense One of the biggest advantages Tennessee could have entering Sunday's matchup is the Cowboys' struggles against the run. They rank last in the NFL in rushing defense, allowing 154.1 yards per game. That creates an appealing matchup for a Titans rushing attack that has shown signs of improvement in recent weeks against other weak run defenses. Tennessee rushed for 141 yards against the Cleveland Browns in Week 7 (26th-ranked run defense) and followed that with 158 rushing yards against Cincinnati (21st-ranked run defense) in Week 8. The Titans also averaged a season-best 6.2 yards per carry collectively against Jacksonville in Week 10. Establishing the ground game early could help Tennessee control possession, keep Dallas' offense off the field, and create more manageable situations for quarterback Cam Ward. 3. Tony Pollard returns to Dallas for the first time since leaving Titans running back Tony Pollard spent the first five years of his career with the Cowboys, as was their full-time starter during his final season with them. Despite his success rushing for over 1000 yards in back-to-back seasons, the Titans prioritized Pollard more than Dallas during his free agency in 2024. Pollard has continued producing in Nashville, recording two additional 1000+ yard seasons and is on pace for his fifth straight year of achieving it with 628 rushing yards through nine games this season. Their defense also gave up 43 points in its overtime loss to the Cincinnati Bengals in Week 8. Those results highlight a potential opportunity for a shootout on Sunday. For Tennessee, the challenge will be finding a way to slow down a Dallas offense that has demonstrated its ability to score against several opposing defenses all season long. 2. The Cowboys have the NFL's worst run defense One of the biggest advantages Tennessee could have entering Sunday's matchup is the Cowboys' struggles against the run. They rank last in the NFL in rushing defense, allowing 154.1 yards per game. That creates an appealing matchup for a Titans rushing attack that has shown signs of improvement in recent weeks against other weak run defenses. Tennessee rushed for 141 yards against the Cleveland Browns in Week 7 (26th-ranked run defense) and followed that with 158 rushing yards against Cincinnati (21st-ranked run defense) in Week 8. The Titans also averaged a season-best 6.2 yards per carry collectively against Jacksonville in Week 10. Establishing the ground game early could help Tennessee control possession, keep Dallas' offense off the field, and create more manageable situations for quarterback Cam Ward. 3. Tony Pollard returns to Dallas for the first time since leaving Titans running back Tony Pollard spent the first five years of his career with the Cowboys, as was their full-time starter during his final season with them. Mayfield has had a rough start to the 2026 campaign with more interceptions (four) than passing touchdowns (three). However, he's still a better option under center than undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels, who took first-team reps in practice Wednesday for the Buccaneers. Daniels, who has already started three games this season due to injury issues for Mayfield, has also thrown for more interceptions (five) than touchdowns (three). Tampa Bay subsequently has not been very proficient through the air this season. In fact, Todd Bowles’ squad ranks league worst in several passing categories: attempts (240), yards (1,277) and touchdowns (six). Meanwhile, on defense, Winfield is one of the Buccaneers’ very best players. A two-time Pro Bowler and one-time All-Pro, the longtime Tampa Bay defender has been especially stout against the run in 2026. The 2020 second-round pick has earned an 85.5 Pro Football Focus grade for his efforts against the run, the 13th-best run-defense mark among 100 qualified safeties. Additionally, he hasn't been too shabby against the pass, and has allowed just five receptions all season. And for his efforts in coverage, he's earned a 67.7 grade from PFF, the 24th-best pass-coverage mark among all qualified safeties. Consequently, the Buccaneers, which stand at just 3-6, would hardly be in an optimal situation playing without both Winfield and Mayfield on Sunday. As for the Lions, they will be down two of their defensive captains and very best players in Week 11: LB Jack Campbell (neck) and EDGE Aidan Hutchinson (ACL). Hutchinson has already been ruled out for the rest of the season, while Campbell is highly unlikely to suit up again in 2026. Detroit, however, is getting back its All-Pro safety for its tilt with Tampa Bay: Kerby Joseph. Joseph – who was activated off the physically unable to perform list Wednesday – hasn't played a single snap since Week 6 of the 2025 season due to a lingering knee issue. Per Lions head man Dan Campbell, Joseph will be on a “pitch count” Sunday, but is still expected to log more snaps than fellow safety Brian Branch did when he returned from his Achilles’ tear earlier this season. Branch played 45 total defensive snaps in his season debut in Week 7 against the Green Bay Packers. Prior to Joseph's chronic knee ailment , he was a ball-hawk safety. In 55 career games, he's secured 20 interceptions, including a league-high nine during his All-Pro campaign in 2024. If he can come even remotely close to replicating that level of production, he'll provide a big boost to the back-end of the Lions’ defense. At this present juncture, I'll give Detroit a 76 percent chance to capture the Week 11 victory. Gilberto Manzano , NFL Staff Writer Iain MacMillan , Senior Editor, Betting Peter Dewey , Associate Managing Editor, Betting All odds listed are via DraftKings Sportsbook Gilberto Manzano Week 11 Upset Pick Tampa Bay Buccaneers (+215) vs. Detroit Lions It didn’t go well for me last week betting against the Lions. But this time it will be different! Remember, a broken clock is right twice a day. Anyway, Detroit will have a few challenges in this one, including facing a tough Tampa Bay defense a week after having to play a game in Germany. The Lions’ explosive offense had trouble generating points against Green Bay, Minnesota, and Miami (the Dolphins!) before bouncing back against the Patriots last week. Perhaps Buccaneers coach Todd Bowles could use some of those blueprints to slow down star running back Jahmyr Gibbs. Also, this will be the Lions’ first game without star edge rusher Aidan Hutchinson, who sustained a season-ending knee injury against the Patriots. Peter Dewey Week 11 Upset Pick Baltimore Ravens (+114) vs. Carolina Panthers If you’re going to make a case for an upset this week where there are five teams favored by double digits, I don’t mind targeting the Baltimore Ravens in their clash with the Carolina Panthers. Carolina barely came away with a win over a bad New Orleans team in Week 10, and it remains pretty banged up on both sides of the ball. The Panthers are a top-10 team in the league in EPA/Play on offense, but they’re in the middle of the pack in EPA/Play on the defensive side of the ball. Carolina is also allowing 4.4 yards per carry on the ground, so this could be the week Derrick Henry gets going. The Ravens are coming off a pretty huge loss at home against the Los Angeles Chargers on Monday night, but Jacoby Brissett wasn’t bad in that matchup, and he may have led this Baltimore team to a win had Zay Flowers not lost a costly fumble late in the fourth quarter. I don’t think that any team in the NFC South should be trusted as a favorite, as the division as a whole is just 4-17 against the AFC North over the last four seasons and 63-111 overall against non-NFC South teams during that stretch. Iain MacMillan Week 11 Upset Pick The Lions' already bad and injured defense continues to take big hits. Now it's their star pass-rusher, Aidan Hutchinson, who is out for the season after celebrating a sack against the Patriots on Sunday. He joins a list that includes D.J. Reed, Kerby Joseph, Devin White, and Jack Campbell, who are on the injured list. It's enough to convince me that now is the time to sell your Lions' stock. Detroit now has to take on a Buccaneers team that's fresh off a BYE week, and that ranks in the top five in both opponent EPA per play and opponent success rate. While the Lions' offense is certainly elite, they're going to struggle to rack up the amount of points they need to aid their limping defense. Baker Mayfield's injury status is up in the air, which could make this bet tough to win, but if he plays, we're in a great spot. Even if he doesn't, Tampa Bay can win this game with their defense and rushing attack alone. They're my upset pick of the week. away.blurb: Mayfield’s availability remains the central variable. If he can return, the Buccaneers gain their veteran starter for an important NFC road test. If he cannot, Daniels’ legs, decision-making, and ability to avoid costly possessions will determine whether Tampa Bay can make its rushing attack the centerpiece of a credible upset bid. – The Lions placed linebacker Jack Campbell (neck) on injured reserve, while edge rusher Aidan Hutchinson (knee) is out for the season. Those absences could make Daniels’ scrambling ability and Tampa Bay’s ground game more consequential if the rookie starts. Buccaneers’ Keionte Scott Earns Rookie Recognition, but One Flaw Stands Out Tampa Bay Buccaneers quarterback Baker Mayfield (leg) has an uncertain outlook for Sunday’s (Nov. 22) road game against the Detroit Lions, creating the possibility rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels will make another start. The Buccaneers need Mayfield’s status clarified quickly because Daniels’ mobility could change the offense’s approach in a matchup expected to hinge on controlling possession, protecting the football, and keeping Detroit’s high-powered attack off the field. Locked On Bucs host James Yarcho said Daniels took the first-team reps after Mayfield missed Wednesday’s practice. The official team preview also listed Mayfield’s lower-leg injury as a major question for the week and noted Tampa Bay promoted Easton Stick from the practice squad, underscoring the need for quarterback insurance. Daniels has started three games while Mayfield was sidelined. He has supplied a dimension the offense can use if he starts again. He has rushed 22 times for 123 yards, a 5.6-yard average, while completing 60 of 98 passes for 501 yards, three touchdowns, and five interceptions. Yarcho does not suggest Daniels is the more polished passer, but rather his ability to escape the pocket could extend drives against a Lions defense missing key front-seven pieces. That mobility matters most if it helps running back Bucky Irving sustain Tampa Bay’s preferred game script. Irving has 825 rushing yards and seven rushing touchdowns through nine games, and the Buccaneers have leaned on him heavily during their recent stretch. A Daniels start would put more pressure on the offense to pair designed quarterback movement, play-action and a disciplined rushing attack rather than asking the rookie to win a pass-heavy game from the pocket. – Irving remains the offensive centerpiece, but the Buccaneers have also discussed reducing his workload after he logged 111 carries over the previous five games. Kenny Gainwell and Sean Tucker could take on more work if Tampa Bay wants to preserve Irving while maintaining its physical identity. – Detroit running back Jahmyr Gibbs presents the defining test for the defense after reaching 1,000 rushing yards in nine games. home.headline: Lions' Aidan Hutchinson Breaks Silence After Knee Injury on Celebration, 'Honestly Can't Believe It'
home.blurb: The play Hutchinson got hurt on was devastating for both teams. It started with him sacking Drake Maye, who left with an ankle injury that could keep him out for the remainder of the season. Hutchinson got up fine at the end of the play, but did a leaping celebration afterward where his knee buckled. He was diagnosed with a torn ACL that will keep him out for the rest of the season. Detroit Lions star Aidan Hutchinson is officially retiring his jumping celebration after suffering a season-ending ACL injury against the New England Patriots on Sunday. In his first public comments since the injury, Hutchinson wrote on Instagram he "honestly can't believe it" happened because he has jumped on a football field "hundreds of times" over the course of his life. Hutchinson closed his statement writing it will be the "last time I go airborne" along with a message to his Lions teammates: "Hold down the fort til I'm back, boys." A two-time Pro Bowler, Hutchinson is tied for second on the Lions with six sacks this season. He also ranks first on the team with 19 quarterback hits and tied for second with six tackles for loss. The Lions (7-2) are in a three-way tie with the Minnesota Vikings and Chicago Bears for first place in the NFC North. They will host the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Ford Field on Sunday.

home.headline: Lions release initial injury report vs. Buccaneers: DJ Reed returns
home.blurb: Starting center Cade Mays (ankle) did not practice. Starting cornerback DJ Reed (hip) returned to practice, but he was a limited participant. Reed has missed each of the Lions' past two games, and the 5-foot-9, 190-pound corner didn't practice either week. Linebacker Joe Bachie (knee), cornerback Khalil Dorsey (ankle), defensive lineman Tyler Lacy (shoulder), cornerback Ennis Rakestraw (shoulder), and running back Sione Vaki (ankle) were also all limited participants. As the Detroit Lions (7-2) gear up for Sunday's showdown against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers (3-6), the team released their initial injury report ahead of the matchup. The Lions activated safety Kerby Joseph on Wednesday. Joseph, who has been working back from a chronic knee injury, was a full participant in the Lions ' initial injury report. home.headline: Report: Lions' Hutchinson out for season with ACL injury
home.blurb: "Nothing new," Lions coach Dan Campbell said after the game when asked for an update on Hutchinson. "We’ll know more when we get back to the States. But any time you lose a player of his caliber, the type of teammate he is — he’s a captain of ours — that doesn’t make things easy. But I thought guys stepped up in his wake and showed up for us today and helped us out." This article originally appeared on The Detroit News: Report: Lions' Hutchinson out for season with ACL injury Initial tests on Aidan Hutchinson’s injured knee showed the Detroit Lions star has a torn ACL, according to a report from NFL Network on Monday, Nov. 16. Hutchinson, 26, had initial tests performed in Germany, where the Lions beat the New England Patriots on Sunday, and will have more done in the United States, the report added. On Good Morning Football, NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport said, “my understanding, the belief is it’s a torn ACL and more for Aidan Hutchinson.” The injury to Hutchinson occurred in the first quarter of Detroit’s win over the Patriots. Hutchinson sacked quarterback Drake Maye and leapt into the air to celebrate. He fell to the ground after landing and grabbed his right knee. Hutchinson, who has six sacks this season, eventually walked off the field under his own power. He entered the blue medical tent on the sideline and remained there for a few moments before later walking to the locker room with trainers at his side. Campbell is scheduled to hold a news conference on Tuesday. If the report from NFL Network is correct and Hutchinson does have a torn ACL, D.J. Wonnum and rookie Derrick Moore would be expected to see an uptick in responsibilities. Wonnum has six sacks this season, and Moore has four over his last two games.

Live Simms Unbuttoned Brian Hamilton , Brian Hamilton The Arizona Cardinals (3-7) travel to Arrowhead Stadium to take on the Kansas City Chiefs (7-2) on Sunday for a matchup between teams heading in completely opposite directions. The Cards are floundering, battling an inordinate number of injuries at the skill positions, and now starting rookie Carson Beck at quarterback. Meanwhile, Patrick Mahomes has the Chiefs in first in the AFC West and just one game behind Buffalo for the top spot in the AFC (Spoiler Alert: the Bills and Chiefs play on Thanksgiving on NBC/Peacock .) It should come as no surprise that the statistical gap is significant: the Cardinals average just 18.4 points per game while allowing 28.9, whereas Kansas City scores 26.3 per game and owns one of the league’s stingiest defenses at 17.3 points allowed per game…and KC is undefeated at home this season (4-0). The Cardinals are coming off an ugly 34-6 home loss to the Los Angeles Rams, a game in which their offense essentially disappeared after the opening quarter. Two 49-yard field goals from Chad Ryland gave Arizona a 6-3 lead, but those would be its only points. Beck, making his first NFL start, completed 11 of 18 passes for 108 yards with two interceptions, while the Cardinals managed only 142 total yards, 34 rushing yards and six first downs. They went 0-for-6 on third down and held the ball for just 17:37. Trey McBride led the team with five catches for 37 yards. The Chiefs delivered a performance that was basically the exact opposite of that put forth by the Cards. KC rolled past the Atlanta Falcons 35-13 for their second straight win. Mahomes was sensational, completing 22 of 35 passes for 348 yards and five touchdowns without throwing an interception. Rookie Emmett Johnson carried the ball 22 times for 101 yards and also caught a touchdown pass, helping Kansas City pile up 461 yards of total offense. The Kansas City defense forced two turnovers and held Atlanta to one touchdown in five red-zone trips. These teams do not meet often, but the recent regular-season history decidedly favors Kansas City. The Chiefs have won the last two meetings, including a 44-21 victory at Arizona in the 2022 season opener, when Mahomes threw five touchdown passes, and a 26-14 win at Arrowhead Stadium in 2018; the Cardinals’ last regular-season victory in the series was 17-14 in 2014.
