picks.headline: Chiefs-Cardinals betting line & prediction: Kansas City’s biggest mismatch yet?
picks.blurb: Read our AI Policy. Kansas City enters 7-2, while Arizona has lost two straight to fall to 3-7. The betting line lists the Chiefs as 15.5-point favorites over the Cardinals. The prediction picks Kansas City to beat Arizona 33-9 and cover the spread. The Kansas City Chiefs won their second game in a row Sunday when they overpowered the Atlanta Falcons 35-13 , improving to 7-2 on the NFL season. The Arizona Cardinals lost their second straight 34-6 to the Los Angeles Rams to drop to 3-7. Here’s what to know about their matchup on Sunday ... How to watch Cardinals at Chiefs Kickoff: Noon Central Where: Arrowhead Stadium in Kansas City TV: CBS (Channel 5 in Kansas City) Radio: KFNZ (96.5 FM in Kansas City, KNSS 98.7 FM in Wichita) Betting line: Chiefs -15.5 Behind the ARI-KC matchup While the Chiefs were getting back on track by taking care of business against the New York Jets and Atlanta Falcons over the past two weeks, the Cardinals have been falling apart at the seams. Sunday’s monumental mismatch starts at the quarterback position, where rookie Carson Beck is expected to make his second career start after completing just 11 of 18 passes for 108 yards and two interceptions against the Rams. Arizona has turned to Beck after trading Jacoby Brissett to the Baltimore Ravens and watching last year’s Chiefs backup Gardner Minshew tear the UCL in his throwing arm. Understanding the reality of the situation, linebacker Drue Tranquill showed the two-time national champion with Georgia some respect before outlining the problems he may face against a Chiefs defense that has come alive with eight sacks over the last two games. “He’s obviously got winning pedigree — he did it in college,” Tranquill said of Beck. “He’ll get another start under his belt this week in a great environment, so it’s a good opportunity for him, but we’ll have to execute our pre-snap looks, have to execute our game plan in terms of owning our leverage, taking away options he might want to go to early in the down. And then hopefully, as the game progresses, we can get the pass rush going, get them in known passing situations and get them on the ground.” With running back Jeremiyah Love, the No. 3 overall pick, on injured reserve, the Cardinals’ best path to an upset is extending possessions with veteran back Tyler Allgeier and utilizing first-team All-Pro tight end Trey McBride. McBride has managed 78 catches for 635 yards and five touchdowns despite Arizona’s struggles. With wide receivers Kendrick Bourne (tibia) and Michael Wilson (neck) out for the remainder of the season, that’s left McBride as Beck’s lone viable option. Among Arizona’s available players, tight end Elijah Higgins ranks second on the team in receiving yards with 18 catches for 162 yards. “They’ve got some good tight ends, and so we’ll have to be on it,” Tranquill said. “They’re big, they’re physical, can make contested catches. And so we’ll have to own our leverage and be physical at the top of the stem and not allow them to create separation, and try to get the ball off these guys.” Arizona’s protection has allowed 28 sacks this season — tied for the sixth-most in the league. Meanwhile, Chiefs defensive lineman George Karlaftis enters Sunday with at least one sack in each of his last three games , Ashton Gillotte is in the midst of a two-game sack streak and Chris Jones has registered 2.5 sacks over the last two games. The Cardinals’ offensive line is a point to watch, as they played against the Rams without starting center Hjalte Froholdt (concussion) and left tackle Jayden Williams (knee), who had already replaced left tackle Paris Johnson Jr. (biceps tear). Both Froholdt and Williams were limited in practice Wednesday. The situation doesn’t get any easier for the Cardinals on the other side of the ball. In the run game, the Cardinals allow 4.2 yards per carry, and through the air, they give up 8.2 yards per pass attempt. The Chiefs opted to rest Kenneth Walker last Sunday against the Falcons because of groin tightness, and he didn’t practice Wednesday . That means rookie Emmett Johnson could make his second straight start after compiling 171 scrimmage yards and two touchdowns in Atlanta. Quarterback Patrick Mahomes is coming off his best passing stat line of the season, in which he threw for 348 yards and five touchdowns against the Falcons. But bigger than that were the chunk gains, as the outing included seven completions of 20 yards or more. While the Cardinals’ secondary is susceptible to explosive passing plays, if there is one area of concern for the Chiefs, it’s that they’re more than capable of generating pressure. Led by safety Budda Baker with 3.5 sacks and outside linebackers Zaven Collins and Josh Sweat with three apiece, the Cardinals have registered 21 sacks this season. “They do a great job of causing havoc and causing pressure, and they do a great job throughout a lot of these football games of kind of stopping the offenses,” Mahomes said. “There’s been parts where offenses have kind of found the big plays, and it has to come within rhythm. It’s not like you can kind of hunt those things. You have to get the ball out of your hand, because if you don’t, they’ll get home, and they’ll cause negative plays.” Protection will be imperative for what could be a shorthanded Chiefs offensive line. Right tackle Jaylon Moore (ankle) and right guard Trey Smith (concussion) both missed practice Wednesday, and it remains to be seen whether newly signed veteran Fred Johnson can provide a boost after joining Kansas City’s practice squad Tuesday. In his opening game in a Kansas City uniform , wide receiver Josh Downs turned 11 snaps into four catches for 53 yards and a touchdown. Wide receiver Rashee Rice led the Chiefs with 82 yards, and Downs, Andrew Armstrong and rookie Cyrus Allen all reached the end zone. Sunday’s game will give way to a short Thanksgiving week for the Chiefs, with perhaps their most important game of the season awaiting them Thursday night against the Buffalo Bills. Given the grand disparity between the two clubs, look for head coach Andy Reid to be mindful about how long he plays some of his key contributors, especially those dealing with injuries. Cardinals-Chiefs game prediction In my 13 years analyzing and previewing Chiefs games, I’m not sure that I can recall a matchup this lopsided going in. But as they say, that’s why they play the games. away.headline: The Chiefs face a rare in-season opportunity with the Cardinals coming to KC
away.blurb: The Cardinals are without their leading wide receiver, Michael Wilson, who injured his back earlier this month and is out for the season. And first-round pick Jeremiyah Love, the running back, is on injured reserve because of an ankle issue. The Chiefs are 16- to 16.5-point favorites against the Cardinals on Sunday. Arizona has lost its last two games by a combined score of 51-9. The Chiefs may rest injured players before playing the Bills on Thanksgiving. You don’t have to be a soothsayer to know that Chiefs coach Andy Reid will be looking forward to the challenge of playing the Arizona Cardinals on Sunday at Arrowhead Stadium. It’s what Reid says each week about the Chiefs’ next opponent. The oddsmakers aren’t so sure it’ll be a challenge for the Chiefs. BetMGM has the Chiefs as a 16-point favorite , while DraftKings has the line at 16 1/2 points . It’s rare to see a team be favored by more than two scores, but that’s where things stand. And it makes for an interesting and rare NFL opportunity facing the Chiefs: Should they rest players Sunday because of a short turnaround into their next game? After playing the Cardinals, the Chiefs will take on the AFC-leading Bills in Buffalo on Thanksgiving. The Chiefs will never publicly say they are pondering resting players given the strength of their opponent, but the Cardinals, 3-7, are down on their luck. After picking up road wins against the Chargers, Rams and Cowboys through the first eight weeks of the season, Arizona has lost its last two games by a combined score of 51-9. Ahead of the NFL trade deadline, the Cardinals dealt their top quarterback (Jacoby Brissett) and wide receiver (Marvin Harrison Jr.). There were 15 players listed on the Cardinals’ injury report last week ahead of Arizona’s game against the Los Angeles Rams. That includes safety Andrew Wingard, who is not expected to play against the Chiefs, according to the team’s website. Four offensive linemen were on that injured list, including Hjalte Froholdt and Jon Gaines II. In the Cardinals’ 34-6 loss to the Rams on Sunday, linebacker Jordan Burch suffered a season-ending knee injury. Rookie Carson Beck will start at quarterback for the Cardinals because backup Gardner Minshew suffered a season-ending injury. Beck has attempted 18 career NFL passes, and his backups are 40-year-old Josh Johnson and rookie Joey Aguilar. The Cardinals will enter Sunday’s game with the 29th-ranked scoring offense and 31st-ranked scoring defense. The Chiefs also have injuries, and a number of players were hurt during Sunday’s game against the Falcons: guard Trey Smith (concussion), tight end Jared Wiley (broken ankle) and Travis Kelce (calf). Also, rookie cornerback Mansoor Delane landed hard on his back. And the Chiefs played without running back Kenneth Walker, who has a groin injury. Regardless of what the oddsmakers say, no game is a gimme, but the Chiefs might have enough firepower against a short-handed Cardinals team that they could let Walker rest.

(KCTV) - As the Kansas City Chiefs prepare for a matchup with the wounded and woeful Arizona Cardinals (3-7), they’ll do so Friday with some question as to who will play quarterback for their opponent. Beck has dealt with the injury throughout the season, but the injury comes days after the 2026 third-round pick made his first career NFL start and was sacked five times by the Los Angeles Rams. If Beck can’t play, veteran Josh Johnson would be in line to make a start for the 12th time in his decade-long career. The Cardinals signed Johnson after trading Jacoby Brissett to the Baltimore Ravens ahead of the trade deadline last week. Brissett had started the first eight games of the season for Arizona. home.headline: The Chiefs face a rare in-season opportunity with the Cardinals coming to KC
home.blurb: The Cardinals are without their leading wide receiver, Michael Wilson, who injured his back earlier this month and is out for the season. And first-round pick Jeremiyah Love, the running back, is on injured reserve because of an ankle issue. The Chiefs are 16- to 16.5-point favorites against the Cardinals on Sunday. Arizona has lost its last two games by a combined score of 51-9. The Chiefs may rest injured players before playing the Bills on Thanksgiving. You don’t have to be a soothsayer to know that Chiefs coach Andy Reid will be looking forward to the challenge of playing the Arizona Cardinals on Sunday at Arrowhead Stadium. It’s what Reid says each week about the Chiefs’ next opponent. The oddsmakers aren’t so sure it’ll be a challenge for the Chiefs. BetMGM has the Chiefs as a 16-point favorite , while DraftKings has the line at 16 1/2 points . It’s rare to see a team be favored by more than two scores, but that’s where things stand. And it makes for an interesting and rare NFL opportunity facing the Chiefs: Should they rest players Sunday because of a short turnaround into their next game? After playing the Cardinals, the Chiefs will take on the AFC-leading Bills in Buffalo on Thanksgiving. The Chiefs will never publicly say they are pondering resting players given the strength of their opponent, but the Cardinals, 3-7, are down on their luck. After picking up road wins against the Chargers, Rams and Cowboys through the first eight weeks of the season, Arizona has lost its last two games by a combined score of 51-9. Ahead of the NFL trade deadline, the Cardinals dealt their top quarterback (Jacoby Brissett) and wide receiver (Marvin Harrison Jr.). There were 15 players listed on the Cardinals’ injury report last week ahead of Arizona’s game against the Los Angeles Rams. That includes safety Andrew Wingard, who is not expected to play against the Chiefs, according to the team’s website. Four offensive linemen were on that injured list, including Hjalte Froholdt and Jon Gaines II. In the Cardinals’ 34-6 loss to the Rams on Sunday, linebacker Jordan Burch suffered a season-ending knee injury. Rookie Carson Beck will start at quarterback for the Cardinals because backup Gardner Minshew suffered a season-ending injury. Beck has attempted 18 career NFL passes, and his backups are 40-year-old Josh Johnson and rookie Joey Aguilar. The Cardinals will enter Sunday’s game with the 29th-ranked scoring offense and 31st-ranked scoring defense. The Chiefs also have injuries, and a number of players were hurt during Sunday’s game against the Falcons: guard Trey Smith (concussion), tight end Jared Wiley (broken ankle) and Travis Kelce (calf). Also, rookie cornerback Mansoor Delane landed hard on his back. And the Chiefs played without running back Kenneth Walker, who has a groin injury. Regardless of what the oddsmakers say, no game is a gimme, but the Chiefs might have enough firepower against a short-handed Cardinals team that they could let Walker rest.

home.blurb: Wiley was carted to the locker room during the first quarter of the blowout win over the Falcons. The team dealt with a few more injuries as the game went on. Reid confirmed that Creed Humphrey got poked in the eye, which was clear on TV. He finished the game and will ultimately be ok. As for CB Mansoor Delane, it seems like he was pulled more so out of an abundance of caution. "He landed on his back and kind of up on that shoulder area," Reid said. "I think he was scared more than anything. He's going to be alright, though." Another injury setback for Delane's shoulder would be troubling, but he sounds like he avoided anything serious. As for Wiley, this is the type of injury that could prematurely end his Chiefs career. As a rookie out of TCU in 2024, Wiley suffered a season-ending ACL injury during practice. That injury really took away the remainder of his rookie season and limited him during the 2025 NFL season as well. It wasn't until this offseason that he felt like he was getting back to himself. However, that never really came to fruition in on-field production. Now, with the ankle fracture that will almost certainly end his season, Wiley is heading for another long rehab and recovery. A fourth-round pick in the 2024 NFL Draft out of TCU, Wiley is listed at 6-foot-6 and 250 pounds. The Chiefs have appeared in 50 combined regular-season and postseason games since the start of the 2024 NFL season. Whether it has been injury or a healthy scratch, Wiley has played in 15 of 50 possible games during that timeframe. Wiley is likely slated for IR with the fractured ankle, with eight more games left in the 2026 NFL regular season. As for how the team will adapt to Wiley's loss, it likely opens a needed roster spot, with Omarr Norman-Lott slated to return soon . Kansas City has three tight ends on the 53-man roster currently, with Travis Kelce, Noah Gray, and Jake Briningstool. They have one tight end on the practice squad in the International Player Pathway Program, Thomas Odukoya. picks.headline: Steelers vs. Eagles bold predictions for NFL Week 11
picks.blurb: Steelers vs. Eagles bold predictions for NFL Week 11 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football Texans cruise on TNF Curt Cignetti slams report Trump pardons Pete Rose Puka Nacua suspended 3 games 'GTA 6' impacts sports Steelers vs. Eagles bold predictions for NFL Week 11 Douglas Fritz, ClutchPoints · ClutchPoints Tue, November 17, 2026 at 6:24 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Pittsburgh Steelers are hurting in the pride department. Meanwhile, the Philadelphia Eagles are just trying to find their way out of a losing streak. Here are bold predictions as these rivals meet in NFL Week 11. It's weird to write off the Steelers. They have a record of 6-3 and are strongly favored to improve to 7-3 against the weak Eagles. It seems like forever since the Eagles won a game. They beat the Commanders and Titans in tight wins to open the 2026 season before embarking on their current seven-game losing streak. Let's look at what to expect as these teams meet. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Steelers QB Aaron Rodgers will throw for 225-plus yards with two TDs The Steelers need to re-establish their passing game. They could handle the Eagles by just pounding them on the ground. But this is an opportunity to restore confidence in the passing attack. Rodgers is coming off games with 172 and 143 passing yards. The latter came in an absolute beatdown at the hands of the Bengals. The Steelers need to have good things happen through the air. Rodgers seemed to call out receiver DK Metcalf after the Bengals debacle, according to a post on X by Andrew Fillipponi. "They had a nice plan for some of the run stuff, but they played press coverage, they played a lot of man coverage, and we didn't make them pay at all," Rodgers said after the game. Nobody is going to confuse the 2026 Rodgers with the one who dominated in the past. However, he played well enough for the Steelers to get to 6-2 before the Bengals game. There's reason to believe he can keep this team ahead of the pack when the opponent isn't overwhelming. The Steelers have no chance in the postseason, but they can get there with six more winnable games left on the schedule: Eagles, Texans, Ravens (twice), Panthers, and Titans. Of course, the Steelers will have to make up for the loss of guard Mason McCormick, who suffered a gruesome ankle injury on Sunday night. Head coach Mike McCarthy said there's a plan, according to the Steelers' YouTube page via Yahoo. "Spencer's, you know, he's just a 360 football player, in my view," McCarthy said. "You know, he started out in his right guard and then also the ability to play left guard. He's a gifted football player. This will be his opportunity." Steelers WR DK Metcalf will get 90-plus yards receiving Metcalf has only topped this mark twice this year. He had 115 yards against the Browns and 93 in an overtime game against the Buccaneers. But this is a spot where he could shine again. The Eagles have been middle of the pack against the pass, but they're trending way down overall as a team. There's a good reason for the Steelers to get Metcalf more involved. It not only matters for Rodgers and the team, but the organization has to deal with his five-year, $150 million contract. Oops. If they don't get Metcalf rolling, they may have to look at trying to get out of his contract. That could prove difficult , according to Sports Illustrated. "Cutting or trading Metcalf with a pre-June 1 designation next offseason would make minimal sense, as doing so would incur a dead money hit of $35.775 million while only opening up $2.650 million in cap space for the 2027 campaign (per Over the Cap)," Jack Markowski wrote. "Cutting or trading Metcalf with a post-June 1 designation in 2027 would save $26.5 million against the cap, however, while also forcing the Steelers to take on $11.925 million in dead money." That's just a lot of ugly numbers. Instead, the Steelers are better off trying to feed Metcalf and see if they can restore the roar he had earlier in his career. Eagles QB Joe Milton will throw for 200-plus yards The Eagles need to see what they have in the young quarterback. He completed only 18 of 34 passes for 169 yards against the Giants. But he also rushed nine times for 64 yards. There's something to like about Milton, but he needs to show better accuracy during this audition that could last for the remainder of the season. Milton reviewed his own performance against the Giants, according to philadelphiaeagles.com. "For my first game here, I feel like I did all right," Milton said. "There are a lot of things that I can clean up as far as protection, just helping those guys out with protection. That's something that we're going to get better (at) this week coming up for sure. "I felt blessed, more blessed. That's about it. I felt more blessed than anything. I was able to see my family in the stands, so it was great, but it was also just great to be out there with the guys that I've been here training with for the past three weeks and learning. And just that communication and connection that the team has, and just being a part of it. I love it. It's great. I wouldn't ask for no better situation than this." It won't be easy against the Steelers' tough defense. But look for Milton to battle through for a good game. That's especially true if he can make a big play early. Confidence is an important part of the equation for a young QB. I like Milton to make more plays with his legs, as he did vs NYG (9/64). It may be a better strategy than running Barkley between the tackles. Goedert has caught 4+ passes in L5. I can't explain what happened to DK Metcalf. 35 catches in nine games is far less than I expected, and I think Steelers fans would agree. Live Simms Unbuttoned Brian Hamilton , Brian Hamilton The Pittsburgh Steelers (6-3) head to Lincoln Financial Field on Sunday for a game against their instate rival, the Philadelphia Eagles (2-7). Although on the road, this game comes at a critical point in the Steelers’ season. With games the next three weeks against the Broncos, the Texans, and the Jaguars - all teams contending for a playoff spot in the AFC - this one is a near must-win against the Birds. Second in the AFC North and sixth in the AFC overall, Aaron Rodgers and co. are a half-game ahead of the Browns and 1.5 games ahead of the Patriots in the postseason chase. The Eagles have struggled for most of the season. Jalen Hurts led Philly to wins in their first two games, but the Eagles have since lost every game as well as their quarterback (blood clots). This season, the Steelers have leaned on Rodgers, a productive running game and a defense that ranks among the league leaders in sacks and turnover differential. The veteran signal-caller has thrown for 2,014 yards with 15 touchdowns and six interceptions, while Jaylen Warren has rushed for 719 yards. Philadelphia’s season has unraveled in large part because of injuries, most notably the aforementioned loss of Hurts to injured reserve with blood clots. That leaves Joe Milton III directing an Eagles offense averaging just 16.4 points and an NFL-low 260.2 yards per game. Pittsburgh’s four-game winning streak came to an abrupt end last Sunday in a 38-18 road loss to Cincinnati. The Bengals completely suffocated the Steelers with Pittsburgh managing only 23 total yards through the first three quarters before producing some offense and points after the game was out of reach. DK Metcalf was held without a catch through three quarters before finishing with two receptions for 54 yards and a touchdown, while the defense spent far too much time on the field. Philadelphia, meanwhile, comes into Sunday’s game rested after its bye but desperately searching for an answer to a disastrous stretch. The Eagles’ most recent game was a 19-11 home loss to the Giants on Nov. 8. Milton made his first Eagles start and completed 18 of 34 passes for just 169 yards. It has been a weekly headline for Philadelphia: “Eagles’ are Offensive on Offense”. The bye, though, may help an injury-ravaged roster: receivers DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) could return after missing the Giants game. Smith’s availability is especially significant because the Eagles badly need another proven weapon alongside Saquon Barkley to make life easier for Milton against a Pittsburgh defense featuring T.J. Watt and one of the NFL’s better pass rushes. Beyond Pittsburgh’s attempt to rebound and Philadelphia’s effort to stop its seven-game skid, the matchup carries a fascinating piece of Pennsylvania rivalry history. The Eagles lead the all-time series 50-29-3, and Pittsburgh has endured an extraordinary drought in Philadelphia. The Steelers have not won in Philly since 1965. They have lost their last 11 games against the Eagles in the City of Brotherly Love. Philadelphia has also dominated the two most recent meetings, winning 27-13 in Philadelphia on Dec. 15, 2024, after a 35-13 home victory in 2022; Pittsburgh’s last win in the series was a 38-29 victory at Heinz Field in 2020. away.headline: Star Pittsburgh Steelers linebacker goes down with thumb injury
away.blurb: Pittsburgh Steelers linebacker Patrick Queen suffered a broken left thumb during the team's game against the Cincinnati Bengals, and Queen intends to play through the injury. He popped up on the injury report with a hand injury Wednesday and was limited at practice. The news was first reported by Chris Halicke of DK Pittsburgh Sports. Queen did not come out of the game once he suffered the injury, and has toughed it out instead. For most of his tenure with the Steelers, Queen has been someone who is willing to play through injuries. The Steelers are dealing with a new injuries coming out of that Bengals game that include Queen, but also outside linebacker Nick Herbig. Herbig was back at practice on Thursday after missing Wednesday's session with hip and rib injuries. home.headline: Eagles get good news on a key target for Joe Milton
home.blurb: DeVonta Smith practiced in full Thursday after being limited Wednesday, according to the Eagles injury report . The receiver has missed five of Philadelphia ’s last six games with a hamstring injury. The Eagles (2-7) host the Pittsburgh Steelers (6-3) on Sunday in a meeting of Pennsylvania’s two NFL teams. Smith said Wednesday that he felt “100 percent” coming out of the bye. The Eagles had not yet listed him as a full participant when he made that comment. Thursday’s report changed that, but the team won’t issue its final game designation until Friday. Head coach Nick Sirianni said Wednesday that Smith and Dontayvion Wicks both had a chance to return. Wicks, who has missed three straight games with an ankle injury, remained limited Thursday. He has 19 catches for 284 yards and a touchdown in his first season in Philadelphia. What Smith’s return would give Milton Sunday’s kickoff at Lincoln Financial Field is set for 1 p.m. ET. The Eagles haven’t had both Smith and Wicks available during Milton’s run as the starter. Friday’s report will show whether he gets one, both, or neither back for Pittsburgh. The Philadelphia Eagles are sticking with Joe Milton III at quarterback after a 19-11 loss to the Giants. The receiving corps he worked with in his first start could look different Sunday. Milton will start again Sunday , Sirianni said. He went 18 of 34 for 169 yards in a 19-11 loss to the New York Giants before the bye. He ran nine times for 64 yards but was sacked seven times and lost a fumble. Saquon Barkley scored Philadelphia’s only touchdown on a three-yard run. Smith has played in only four games, yet he trails Makai Lemon by 2 yards for the team lead in receiving. His 26 catches have gone for 310 yards and two touchdowns. Wicks ranks fourth in receiving yards behind Lemon, Smith and tight end Dallas Goedert. In his last game, Smith caught seven passes for 75 yards and a touchdown against Carolina on Oct. 18. His best game this season came against Tennessee, when he finished with 10 catches for 117 yards and a score in a four-point Eagles win. Philadelphia hasn’t won since. Smith would give Milton another place to go with the ball when the pocket collapses. The Steelers are coming off a 38-18 loss to Cincinnati. T.J. Watt, who practiced in full Thursday after a rest day, and Alex Highsmith give Pittsburgh a threat off either edge. away.headline: Ravens DT Nnamdi Madubuike misses second practice before Panthers game
away.blurb: Baltimore Ravens defensive tackle Nnamdi Madubuike missed practice for a second straight day Thursday with a hamstring injury, while rookie right guard Vega Ioane was upgraded to full participation ahead of Sunday’s game against the Carolina Panthers . Madubuike left Monday night’s 23-20 loss to the Los Angeles Chargers and was ruled out in the third quarter. Coach Jesse Minter said Wednesday the Ravens would evaluate how the hamstring responds later in the week. Ioane was listed as limited on Wednesday’s estimated report with knee and shoulder injuries after leaving the Chargers game in the third quarter. His upgrade is an encouraging sign for an offensive line that helped produce just 16 rushing yards Monday. Safety Jaylinn Hawkins remained limited with a knee injury. Running back Adam Randall (neck and hamstring), tight end Matt Hibner (hand) and outside linebacker Mike Green (biceps) were listed as full participants for a second straight day. Carolina tight ends Darren Waller and Tommy Tremble were listed as limited Thursday with knee injuries after both were listed as nonparticipants Wednesday. Running back Chuba Hubbard returned to full participation after a rest day, and outside linebacker Trevis Gipson (ankle) was upgraded from limited to full. Linebacker Bobby Okereke (foot) and safety Isaiah Simmons (knee) remained out of practice. Young (foot) and cornerbacks Will Lee III (hamstring) and Mike Jackson (groin) were listed as full participants for the second straight day. Jackson remains in his return-to-practice window and would need to be activated from injured reserve to play Sunday. The teams’ Friday reports will provide the official game designations. Cornerback Marlon Humphrey was added to Thursday’s report as a nonparticipant for personal reasons. Minter sent Humphrey home Thursday and said the cornerback will be inactive Sunday. The decision came a day after Humphrey apologized for saying on his podcast that Baltimore was “best at making criminals.” Vega Ioane upgraded to full participation Madubuike’s status is the main injury question for Baltimore heading into Friday. His availability will help determine how the Ravens rotate their interior linemen against Carolina and how much pressure they can generate up the middle against Bryce Young. Humphrey’s absence also changes the coverage rotation against a Panthers receiving group led by Tetairoa McMillan. away.headline: Chargers vs. Ravens Week 10 injury report for Monday Night Football
away.blurb: Before kickoff, let's take a look at the injury report for both teams and which players could be unavailable. The Ravens are in relatively good shape heading into Monday night, with only one player officially ruled out and one listed as questionable. Safety Jaylinn Hawkins is the lone player ruled out, while running back Adam Randall is questionable. That leaves Baltimore in a favorable position compared to its opponent. For the most part, Baltimore should have the majority of its roster available. The biggest concern remains Jackson's absence, which puts even more pressure on Brissett to provide enough offense to keep the Ravens competitive. Wide receiver Ladd McConkey is the biggest name ruled out for Los Angeles. His absence takes away an important piece of the passing game, making life more difficult for an offense that has struggled to find consistency. Five other players are listed as questionable: guard Kayode Awosika, defensive lineman Justin Eboigbe, tight end David Njoku, linebacker Denzel Perryman and offensive tackle Trey Pipkins. The good news is that the rest of the players on the report should be available Monday night, barring any last-minute changes. That gives Los Angeles a chance to avoid an even longer list of absences, but the players already ruled out and those carrying questionable designations could still make an impact. It's difficult to build consistency when important contributors are constantly missing time. McConkey's absence is particularly frustrating because the Chargers need their best offensive weapons available if they want to turn things around. home.headline: Panthers injury report shows more help on the way for the defense
home.blurb: Last week, we talked about the good news of Mike Jackson and Jonathon Brooks fully practicing. It turns out they only took scout team reps and should have been listed as limited participants. Both ended up out for the game against the Saints this past Sunday. Now they are both full participants again, but this time it's for real. Mike Jackson has already said he expects to play this Sunday, which is a huge add for a defense that seems to be turning the corner with new defensive coordinator Todd Wash. He might be joined by rookie Will Lee, who was starting to show flashes before he suffered his own muscle injury. That dup would obviously be a gargantuan upgrade over what the Panthers have had on the outside the last few weeks. No offense. Nnamdi Madubuike – DNP – Hamstring The Ravens' injury report does a disservice to their actual injury woes. Lamar Jackson has had a nightmare season in terms of injuries. He's on injured reserve, and so is backup quarterback Tyler Huntley. The Ravens acquired Jacoby Brissett in an act of desperation, but that hasn't panned out so far. They're relying on newly acquired Cam Jurgens to center the offensive line after they lost several centers to injury over the first few weeks of the season. It turns out he just might not be any good anymore. The Jets are now 2-8 on the season. In one and a half seasons under Aaron Glenn the Jets have a 5-22 record and a 0-9 record in the AFC East. This is not good. This week the Jets were home to take on the Buffalo Bills. They kept it competitive for a little more than a half. At halftime the Jets trailed 10 – 6. The Jets got the ball to start the third quarter. Cade Klubnik took over for an injured Geno Smith and made a few nice plays with his leg and his arm to get the Jets in scoring position. They settled for a field goal to get within a point of the Bills at 10 – 9 early in the third quarter. That was as close as the Jets would get in the game. The Bills outscored the Jets 21 – 3 the rest of the way as Klubnik and the Jets offense were no match for Josh Allen and the Bills offense. The drubbing at the hands of the Bills left the Jets with a 2-8 record to start the season, in 3rd place in the AFC East. Though mathematical elimination is still probably a month or so away, it has become obvious the Jets playoff drought will extend to 16 years and counting by season's end. The Jets are also just one loss away from their 11th straight losing season. The last time the Jets won more than seven games in a season Barack Obama was still President. Now the Jets go on the road to face the only winless team left in the NFL, the Los Angeles Chargers. The Chargers play the Baltimore Ravens on Monday Night Football, so it's possible they will no longer be winless by the time they face the Jets. The Chargers rank dead last in the NFL in points scored, with Justin Herbert somehow crashing to by far the lowest point in his career. After spending his entire career in the vicinity of a top 10 quarterback in the NFL, Herbert has arguably been the worst starting quarterback in the league this year. New Chargers offensive coordinator Mike McDaniels' system appears to be a poor match for Herbert's skill set, and the result has been an offensive train wreck. The Chargers have not scored more than 23 points in any game this season, and they have not allowed less than 22 points in any game this season. It's tough to win games like that, but the Jets may prove to be an elixir for what ails the Chargers. Let's take a look at the current odds for this game according to FanDuel Sportsbook . The oddsmakers think the Chargers will beat the Jets next Sunday. It's come to this: the Jets aren't even favored over a winless team. The current line has the Jets road underdogs by 3.5 points. The game has an over/under of 40.5 points. On the moneyline the Jets are +156 while the Chargers are -186. A loss next Sunday against the Chargers would be just another humiliation for the Jets. Perhaps they can find a way to avoid that fate after being beaten by a winless Dolphins team earlier this season. Perhaps. Perhaps not. Does it really matter in another lost Jets season? J-E-T-S! New York has lost five straight, while Los Angeles finally snapped an 11-game losing streak dating to last season with its first victory of 2026 this past Monday night. The Jets have been the more productive offense statistically, averaging 19.4 points and 341.9 yards per game, compared with a Chargers’ attack sitting last in the league at 16.0 points per game. Still, Los Angeles enters Sunday with a little momentum and actually favored to win. The Jets’ latest setback was a 31-12 home loss to Buffalo, a game that was competitive at halftime before unraveling after the break. New York trailed just 10-6 at intermission and ultimately produced 376 yards, but the offense failed to score a touchdown for the second consecutive game, with Jason Sanders accounting for all 12 points on four field goals. Geno Smith completed 13 of 21 passes for 148 yards but briefly exited for a concussion evaluation before returning and then suffering an ankle injury in the third quarter. Rookie Cade Klubnik made his NFL debut in relief, completing 11 of 20 passes for 137 yards with an interception, while Garrett Wilson caught seven passes for 106 yards and Breece Hall finished with more than 100 yards from scrimmage. Los Angeles, meanwhile, finally found their way into the win column Monday night with a 23-20 road victory over Baltimore, and the formula looked exactly like what Jim Harbaugh wants from his team. The Chargers dominated the line of scrimmage, outrushing Baltimore 160-16. Omarion Hampton led the way with 105 yards and a touchdown on 22 carries. Justin Herbert threw for only 129 yards but played turnover-free football for the first time this season. He added 51 rushing yards, including a 22-yard touchdown on Los Angeles’ opening possession. Cameron Dicker kicked four field goals, and the defense essentially erased Derrick Henry , limiting him to 10 yards on 10 carries despite his two short-yardage touchdowns. away.headline: Is Garrett Wilson Playing Today? (Injury Update, Betting Impact for Bills vs. Jets in NFL Week 10)
away.blurb: Wilson is officially listed as questionable for the AFC East battle with the Buffalo Bills, but he appears to be trending in the right direction to play. Garrett Wilson (concussion) officially listed questionable for Week 10. According to Jets head coach Aaron Glenn, Wilson needs to clear one more step to get out of the consussion protocol, but Glenn believes that will happen in time for Sunday's game. Last week, New York scored just 12 points with Wilson out of the lineup, and it slipped to 16th in the league in EPA/Play on offense as a result. This season, Wilson has appeared in eight of the Jets' nine games, catching 43 passes for 527 yards and three scores. He's played 88.5 percent of the team's offensive snaps, so he'll be out there for almost every play against Buffalo if he's able to go. I do appreciate Coach going out and saying that. He doesn't have to say that, but I do appreciate it." Here's the situation for New York: only one player on their injury report has been listed as "OUT" for Sunday. Backup linebacker Trevin Wallace is dealing with a groin injury and won't suit up. Outside of him, there are eight players listed as game-time decisions. "For guys that will be limited today: Omar (Cooper Jr.), (Joseph) Ossai, Garrett (Wilson), Nashon (Wright). Over the first nine games, New York has seen injuries to Garrett Wilson, Breece Hall, Omar Cooper Jr., their tight ends, and the offensive line. I think Geno's had a really good year, and it would be disrespectful to him to just [replace him]." With Smith returning to practice, even in a limited capacity, the Jets are clearly counting on their established QB1 to lead the offense this Sunday. home.headline: Breaking Down Jets' Injury Outlook to Begin Week 11 (Who's Hurt & Who Could Return vs. Chargers)
home.blurb: Breaking Down Jets' Injury Outlook to Begin Week 11 (Who's Hurt & Who Could Return vs. Chargers) - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Because of the NFL's aggressive and physical nature, it's nearly impossible for a team to finish a game without a player suffering an injury. While injuries are part of the game, some teams sustain more injuries than others, which ultimately affects how their season plays out. Omar Cooper Jr. sustained an ankle injury on the first play and didn't return to the game. Dylan Parham and Geno Smith also suffered injuries and were unable to return. Even though Jarvis Brownlee Jr. was listed as a limited participant on Friday, he was ruled out against the Bills with an illness. The former Louisville Cardinal has had an up-and-down season, recording 11 total tackles and a sack across eight games. If Brownlee is either a full or limited participant in the Jets' upcoming practices, we should expect him to play against the Chargers. Since re-injuring his quad in Week 6 against the Patriots, Mauigoa has been on injured reserve, but he is eligible to return for Week 11's matchup with the Chargers. The Athletic's Zack Rosenblatt reported Friday that Mauigoa was one of seven players on injured reserve who were working out off to the side of practice . This doesn't mean Mauigoa will play next Sunday, but his appearance at practice indicates that he's ramping up and getting closer to making a return. Trevin Wallace was the only player who didn't participate in any of the Jets' practices last week and, as a result, was ruled out for Week 10's matchup due to a groin injury. Although the injury has sidelined him for the past two weeks, it hasn't had major consequences for New York's special teams. Even though Wallace hasn't impressed in this role, recording just three total tackles and earning a 63.9 special teams grade , per Pro Football Focus , the team could use all the contributors it can get after allowing a 95-yard kickoff return for a touchdown to Dylan Laube two weeks ago. If Wallace can be a full participant in any of the team's practices this week, we should anticipate his return to the lineup next Sunday. If Smith is available and practices during the week, we should expect the 14-year veteran to suit up. But if he doesn't, New York will turn to rookie Cade Klubnik as its starter.Although Klubnik showed some flashes, he needs more time and reps before he can be a reliable starter. Tyler Baron (knee), Anez Cooper (shoulder), Marcelino McCrary-Ball (ankle), Max Mitchell (head/concussion), David Onyemata (groin), and T'Vondre Sweat (ACL sprain) are all on the short-term injured reserve list and are eligible to return this season. home.headline: Geno Smith Injury Update, New NFL Rumors on Jets QB's Status Ahead of Chargers Game
home.blurb: New York Jets quarterback Geno Smith will participate in Wednesday's practice in limited capacity after suffering multiple injuries in last Sunday's loss to the Buffalo Bills, head coach Aaron Glenn told reporters. The Jets (2-8) are on track for a high pick in the 2027 NFL draft. Should Smith remain available to start, the Jets may not get a longer look at Klubnik before deciding whether to use that pick on a quarterback. Smith left Sunday's game twice for a concussion evaluation and then for the ankle injury. He will be listed on the injury report with an ankle injury, Glenn said. NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported Monday Smith "underwent tests today that did not reveal anything major." "Smith, whose ankle provided the biggest concern, will continue to be evaluated through the week," Rapoport reported. The Jets are preparing to play Sunday at the Los Angeles Chargers. Glenn confirmed earlier this week Smith will continue starting over Cade Klubnik if healthy. When asked Wednesday if he expected Smith to play against the Chargers, Glenn said , "We'll see how the week goes." Smith left Sunday's game in a golf cart, then visited the X-rays before leaving without visible crutches or walking boot, per ESPN's Rich Cimini . ESPN's Jeremy Fowler reported Smith "was in pain Sunday but showed signs of improvement Monday, giving confidence that he will try to push through and play Sunday vs. Los Angeles." SNYs Connor Hughes reported the Jets shut down offers at the trade deadline for Smith, who has completed 67.1 percent of his passes with 2,226 passing yards to go along with 12 touchdowns and three interceptions in 10 games of his age-36 season. Klubnik saw his first action of the season when he went 11-for-20 with 137 yards after replacing Smith in Sunday's third quarter. He scrambled for another 26 yards while throwing no touchdowns and an interception. ▶️ Full Bills-Jets Recap 05:23 Glenn said Monday he felt it would be "disrespectful" to Smith to consider starting Klubnik in order to conduct more evaluation of the rookie quarterback down the stretch. home.headline: Broncos get boost regarding injuries days before facing Raiders
home.blurb: Coming out of their Week 10 bye, every player on the 53-man roster was present at Wednesday’s practice, including several key contributors who have been dealing with injuries. Related Articles NFL Calls Out NBC’s Mike Florio for On-Air Joke About Mike Vrabel The Denver Broncos could be getting some massive reinforcements at just the right time. Wide receiver Jaylen Waddle, cornerbacks Riley Moss and Kris Abrams-Draine, and safeties Talanoa Hufanga and Brandon Jones were all back on the field as Denver prepares for its AFC West showdown with the visiting Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday. Waddle and Moss are the biggest developments as both suffered concussions during Denver’s Week 9 win over the Carolina Panthers. Neither player finished that game, leaving the Broncos without two important pieces on opposite sides of the ball. Getting Waddle back would give quarterback Bo Nix another explosive receiving threat and Moss would help restore Denver’s starting cornerback pairing alongside Patrick Surtain II. Hufanga could also provide a massive boost to the defense. An ankle injury has kept him sidelined since the Broncos’ Week 5 matchup against the Los Angeles Chargers. Hufanga already has 23 total tackles, three pass breakups, two interceptions (including a pick-six) and a forced fumble in just five games this season. More news : Aaron Rodgers Could Get 2 Key Weapons Back for Steelers-Eagles Showdown The timing couldn’t be better for Denver. The Broncos enter Week 11 with a 7-2 record and a five-game winning streak, sitting among the top teams in the AFC. They’ll host the 4-6 Raiders at Empower Field at Mile High, looking to extend their run to six straight wins and strengthen their position in the AFC West. Las Vegas is coming off two straight losses and will be looking to get back on track, making it an important opportunity for Denver to protect its position in the division. Raiders rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza is still searching for his first win as Vegas’ starter. More news : Vikings Get Some Good News on Jordan Addison After Injury Scare More news : Nick Sirianni Makes Decision on Eagles OC Sean Mannion Amid Offensive Struggles Having five injured players back at practice is certainly encouraging, but none of them have been cleared for Sunday’s game. Waddle and Moss still have to complete the NFL ‘s concussion protocol before they can play, but the fact that they’re back at practice indicates that will probably happen in the next few days. Still, after a bye week that gave several players extra time to recover, the Broncos have plenty of reason to be optimistic heading into a crucial divisional clash. picks.blurb: 5 Bold Predictions for Jaguars-Giants: Bhayshul Tuten's Field Day Skip to main content SI.COM Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code Fanatics Sportsbook Promo Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Rainbet Promo Code Stake Promo Code PREDICTION MARKETS College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code Novig Promo Code Underdog Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- The Jacksonville Jaguars are set to take on the New York Giants in one of Week 11's most interesting matchups, and there is plenty at stake for both teams. For the 7-2 Jaguars, they are fighting to secure the AFC South for the second year in a row, as well as fighting for a top seed in a tight AFC playoff race. To beat the Giants, who have exceeded expectations in their first year under John Harbaugh, the Jaguars will need to be at their best. So, how do we see the Jaguars' big test against the Giants playing out? We break it down with this week's bold predictions. Bhayshul Tuten Hits 100 Yards Rushing No running back has hit 100 yards rushing in a game against the Giants this season, though Kyren Williams and Blake Corum did combine for 164 rushing yards against them in Week 2. Otherwise, the Gians have limited running backs from making a major impact, allowing just four rushing scores from the position this season. With that said, I think we see Bhayshul Tuten have a field day, even with his recent injury issues. According to NextGenStats, "Tuten has forced a missed tackle on 33.3% of his carries this season, the third-highest rate among running backs with at least 100 carries, behind only Kenneth Walker III (38.0%) and Jahmyr Gibbs (36.7%). He has forced 49 missed tackles on the ground, the fourth-most in the NFL, with 267 of his 609 rushing yards coming after forcing missed tackles (43.8%), the highest share among that same group of backs. Giants' defenders have missed 15.0% of their tackle opportunities this season, the second-highest rate in the NFL behind only the Broncos (17.5%)." Add in Tuten's skill-set against a Giants defense that is not great in terms of making one-on-one tackles, and this suggests it could be a good day for Tuten. But the real reason I have him going over 100 yards is bcause I expect him to get at least 25 carries. The Jaguars' entire offensive identity is being balanced, and running Tuten in heavier packages could be the only way for the Jaguars to get the Giants out of their blitz looks. Jaguars Limit Giants to Under 3.5 YPC The Giants have had something going with their running game lately, with Giants running back/mascot Cam Skattebo turning in his two best games of the season over his last two performances. In Weeks 7 and 10 combined, Skattebo rushed 35 times for 202 yards (5.77 yards per carry) for three touchdowns. He has a limited skill-set, but he has been able to pave the way for the Giants running game. With that in mind, I think we see the Jaguars get back to their elite run defense this week after back-to-back weeks allowing too many chunk yards. I think the difference in talent level between Jordan Davis and the rest of the Jaguars' nose tackle options is significant enough that the addition of Davis to the defensive line this week should make all of the difference. The run defense has not been the same without Davon Hamilton, but now the Jaguars finally have their reinforcement set to debut. Parker Washington Makes Another 50+ Yard Catch No receiver has made bigger plays for the Jaguars this year than Parker Washington, who has been the Jaguars' primary downfield receiver all season. He has caught a 50-yard pass in back-to-back weeks, first for a touchdown in Week 9 and then last week to set up a scoring drive against the Titans. With the way the Giants like to play defense with their cornerbacks, I believe this week could be prime for another big Washington grab. According to NextGen Stats, "Washington has averaged 5.0 yards per route against press coverage this season, the most in the NFL, ahead of Jaxon Smith-Njigba (4.7), Mike Evans (4.6) and Tee Higgins (4.4) among receivers with at least 25 routes against press coverage. Washington has faced press on a team-high 46 routes, drawing 16 targets on those plays (34.8%), the eighth-highest target rate among that same group. He has turned those targets into 229 yards (7th-most) and three touchdowns (T-5th-most), while recording 100 receiving yards over expected, the second-most, trailing only Smith-Njigba (+179). The Giants' defense has pressed at least one cornerback on 70.6% of their plays this season, the highest rate in the NFL.." The Giants are going to want to play press-man coverage and challenge the Jaguars receivers at the line of scrimmage. This is where Washington has thrived, and where Trevor Lawrence has trusted him time and time again. I expect another day full of big plays from the Jaguars' No. 1 wide receiver. Jaguars Force 3 J.J. McCarthy Turnovers J.J. McCarthy has not been the turnover prone quarterback that he was in Minnesota in his few games with the Giants, throwing two interceptions over the last month. With that in mind, I think this is the week the Jaguars can let the takeaways flow due to the nature of how McCarthy plays. McCarthy is at his best when he is extending plays with his legs and creating outside of the pocket, but the Jaguars' defense as a whole is meant to counter that. The Jaguars' entire defensive scheme is about forcing the ball out of the quarterback's hands quickly, and these are the scenarios where McCarthy's issues with accuracy and decision-making show up the most. I see the Jaguars getting two interceptions and a forced fumble on McCarthy, largely because the Jaguars' style of defense will let McCarthy play right into their hands. He is playing OK, which is far better than what he showed in Minnesota, but I think the Jaguars get after him this week. Jessie Bates III Plays Every Snap Jessie Bates III did not make his Jaguars debut in Week 10 as they opted to give him the bye week he never got in Atlanta this season, which means Sunday vs. the Giants will be the first time we see the All-Pro safety in Jaguars threads. While the Jaguars took their time with letting Bates and Davis hit the field on game day, I believe their let them play big roles this week. Due to the nature of the position, I believe that means Bates will play every single snap at safety next to Antonio Johnson. The Jaguars have gotten by the last few weeks with Rayuan Lane as their No. 2 safety option, but last week's game against the Titans made it clear that he is better as depth and as a role player. There is no reason for the Jaguars to not let Bates play the entire game this week, which will mark 13 days since he was traded for. The Jaguars are set to face their toughest test since the bye week ended with the 5-3-1 New York Giants in Week 11. A game that head coach Liam Coen has already said will have to be won in the trenches will be a challenge the Jaguars haven't faced in Weeks. To preview the Jaguars and Giants clash as Jacksonville prepares for their second-half playoff run, we spoke with Patricia Traina of Giants OnSI to go behind the scenes and get an idea of what the Jaguars can really expect. So, how does Traina see this game from the Giants' perspective, and what will it take for Jacksonville to win? We break it down below. 1) What is Arvell Reese more dangerous at: playing linebacker or rushing the passer? Traina: Both. Overall, Reese ranks third among Giants linebackers (inside and outside) with 14 pressures per NFL+, and he has the second-lowest average time to sack (4.0 seconds) in that group. And the scary thing is that this young man, whose name has been mentioned for Defensive Rookie of the Year honors, is just getting started. Reese as a pass rusher (just 107 times so far) as he has been in coverage (246 times). I would think that as the game continues to slow down for him, he will see an increase in his role. 2) How do you view the matchup between Malik Nabers and Travis Hunter? Traina: I think that’s going to be a key matchup. Offensive coordinator Matt Nagy has done a good job of scheming Nabers open this season by moving him around the formation. When playing in the slot, he has an 84.6% reception rate and has scored both of his touchdowns from the slot. Travis Hunter hasn’t worked much from the slot this season. They have Hunter down as having played six total snaps in the slot, defending just one target that was not completed. I am very interested in seeing how much the Giants put Nabers in the slot on Sunday and, when he’s not in the slot, how much, if any, the Jaguars have Hunter travel with him. 3) How much have the Giants trusted J.J. McCarthy when it comes to attacking defenses downfield? Explosive plays have been one of the Jaguars’ few weaknesses. Traina: Overall, the Giants have a 44.7% passing completion rate (10th in the league) on deep balls of 20+ air yards. This season, McCarthy has a 52.6% completion rate on deep passes of 20+ air yards. As you might guess, Nabers has been the main target on those deep balls., he’s caught 12 of 21 (57.1%) with one drop. Rookie Malachi Fields has caught three of nine, and Darnell Mooney one of six. Tight end Isaiah Likely has caught three of seven deep passes. As I’m guessing the Jaguars will do everything possible to take Nabers out of the equation, I suspect this could be a good opportunity for Fields to have a breakout game. 4) What kind of impact has former Jaguars CB Greg Newsome made in New York? Traina: He’s been outstanding in coverage, so much so that the Giants recently gave him a three-year contract extension. He currently has a career-best 71.2 coverage grade from PFF and has allowed opponents just a 57.6% completion rate. Newsome has also allowed just 61 YAC, has yet to surrender a touchdown, and has five pass breakups, all good for a 63.8 NFL coverage rating, which is the best of his career. 5) If Jacksonville wins this game, what do you think would be the biggest reason why? They make the Giants one-dimensional. The Jaguars have one of the best run defenses in the league right now, and I’m fairly certain they’ll zero in on shutting down running back Cam Skattebo and challenging McCarthy to beat them through the air. McCarthy is 9-4 as a starter in games where his offense has rushed for 100+ yards collectively. That’s not to say McCarthy and the Giants can’t pull off the upset, but if they become one-dimensional, it’ll be that much harder for them to do so. As my readers and listeners have reminded me, the Giants ran up a storm against the Houston Texans a few weeks back, posting a season-high 188 yards against a Texans run defense that was top five going into that game. So yes, the Giants have a chance. Published Nov 19, 2026 JOHN SHIPLEY John Shipley has been covering the Jacksonville Jaguars as a beat reporter and publisher of Jaguar Report since 2019. Q: Why has Trevor Lawrence been so surgical against zone coverage? Jacksonville Jaguars quarterback Trevor Lawrence | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect JS: There are several reasons. He has a group of pass-catchers in Jakobi Meyers, Parker Washington and Brenton Strange who all thrive at beating zone coverage thanks to their ability to find soft spots in zones and work the middle of the field. JS: There are several reasons. He has a group of pass-catchers in Jakobi Meyers, Parker Washington and Brenton Strange who all thrive at beating zone coverage thanks to their ability to find soft spots in zones and work the middle of the field. Liam Coen’s scheme also gives Lawrence and the passing game plenty of open looks against zone coverage, thanks to the balance they play with on offense and how they scheme open wide receivers. But most importantly, it comes down to how Lawrence is playing. He is confident in everything he is doing before and after the snap, far more confident than he has looked in past years. He knows where the ball is going, and he knows how to fit it in there regardless of how open or tight the passing windows are. Jacksonville Jaguars center Robert Hainsey | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect JS: It will likely impact communication. That said, this might not be the crushing loss many outside Jacksonville believe it is. Hainsey has been the Jaguars’ fifth-best offensive lineman this season, and a lot of his value comes pre-snap. There is a real chance the Jaguars could see stronger play from second-year center Jonah Monheim, whom the staff rates extremely highly and who has played well in spot starts for Hainsey in the past. JS: When it comes to the Jaguars’ defense vs. the Giants’ offense, the biggest matchup I am going to be watching is Malik Nabers against Travis Hunter. Hunter has been a true shutdown No. 1 cornerback this season, even beyond his amazing athletic feats on his interceptions. He is the only Jaguars cornerback who can really run with Nabers, and I am fascinated to see these two battle downfield. The Jaguars don’t have their cornerbacks following receivers, but this might be the week to consider it. As for the Jaguars’ offense vs. the Giants’ defense, I am going with Walker Little against Abdul Carter. Little has played well for the Jaguars since stepping in as the starting left tackle a month ago due to injuries, but a player on Carter’s level hasn’t tested him. Little has proven he can get the job done week in and week out, but this week will be about proving that he can handle playing a blue-chip talent, which is exactly what he will need to do during a critical playoff run. They are not flawless, since they still give up some explosive plays, and they do not get a ton of sacks. But Campanile has built one of the best run defenses in the NFL, and his philosophy of forcing quarterbacks to get the ball out of their hands quickly has led to plenty of takeaways and big plays. Campanile should be a future head coach, and the proof is in the pudding: he has helped elevate and evolve the Jaguars’ defense over the past two years. Q: The Jags have been blowing out opponents. What are your expectations for this week, though? I think Trevor Lawrence will still be taking snaps in the fourth quarter this week, which has not been a given most weeks. There is a lot more respect in the Jaguars’ building right now than there was the last time these two teams played in 2022. picks.blurb: NFL predictions: Our picks for Giants-Jaguars, the full Week 11 slate - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football Texans cruise on TNF Curt Cignetti slams report Trump pardons Pete Rose Puka Nacua suspended 3 games 'GTA 6' impacts sports NFL predictions: Our picks for Giants-Jaguars, the full Week 11 slate Ed Valentine · SB Nation Thu, November 19, 2026 at 5:44 PM UTC · 7 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The New York Giants face major test this week when they face the Jacksonville Jaguars. It is also a game that will provide a huge swing in the Giants' expected chances to make the playoffs. Will the Giants upset Jacksonville? See what our Big Blue View staff members think about that game and the rest of the Week 11 action in this week's staff picks. I don't think the Giants win this game. I think there's a path to a win for the Giants, if they can find it. The Giants are one of the very best teams in the NFL at forcing drives to end in punts. At the same time, the Jaguars will be without their starting center and the Giants are one of the best teams in the League at creating quick pressure. That's important because Trevor Lawrence has been one of the quarterbacks most affected by pressure in the NFL. At the same time, the Giants have rediscovered the explosive pass with J.J. McCarthy, which has been the weakness of the Jags' defense. If the Giants can score touchdowns while disrupting Lawrence, they've got the chance to come away with the upset. We've seen the Giants rebound after bad games, as well as play much better than anticipated when they're underdogs. Maybe both will happen here. The flip side of the coin is simpler and scarier to me: The Giants have one of the worst red zone defenses in the NFL, and the Jaguars have one of the best red zone offenses in the league. If the Giants can't stop them between the 20s, this game could get ugly fast. Pick: Jaguars Jacksonville is one of the hottest teams in the league with a young and explosive offense that can run the football. Their defense is aggressive but doesn't NEED to bring the blitz — they blitz at about a league-average rate, but Anthony Campanile does an excellent job utilizing simulated pressure to harass opposing quarterbacks. Jacksonville is third in offensive EPA, 4th in defensive EPA allowed, and 1st in Net EPA — they're a juggernaut based on their performance and the advanced analytics. Still, that doesn't mean the Giants don't have a chance — they just must play efficient football and avoid the catastrophic mistakes that have robbed them of wins. It's possible, but against the most efficient team in the NFL, it will be difficult. John Harbaugh will have the Giants ready and prepared for the game, and I believe it will be more exciting and competitive. Jacksonville is concluding their third straight road game, which could give the Giants a slight advantage at home, but I ultimately believe the better team finds a way to win. David Hartman It took 11 weeks, but for the first time this season, the Giants will face a team with a winning record when the 7-2 Jaguars come to town on Sunday. Not only is Jacksonville running away with the AFC South (they lead the division by four games), but they're steamrolling the competition. They've won their last three games by a combined 75 points. This is easily Big Blue's toughest test of the season, so far. Jacksonville is very good on both sides of the ball. They're fourth in offensive DVOA, third in defensive DVOA, and third in overall DVOA. They also have an excellent field goal kicker with crazy range. If you look at both rosters, it's hard to find clear advantages for the Giants at any position group outside of tight end, and even there, Jacksonville has good players. Can the Giants win this game? Yes. They're at home, they're getting an extra three days of rest, and as we saw when they played Houston, they aren't scared and can surprise as a big underdog. They'll need to dial it up on defense and pressure Trevor Lawrence into the kinds of mistakes he used to make before Liam Coen got there. They also might have a little extra motivation after letting last week's game against the Commanders slip away at the end. I won't be surprised if John Harbaugh's team hangs in there and keeps it as a one-score game most of the way. But in the end, until the Giants show me that they can beat a really good team, I can't pick them to do so. Tony Del Genio You can talk yourself into believing that the Giants can beat Jacksonville this Sunday. They needed a miraculous last-second 57-yard field goal to beat the Eagles team (with Jalen Hurts) that the Giants defeated (without Hurts). They lost to the Texans team that the Giants beat the following week. The woeful Titans were within a TD against them last week with 5 minutes left. So indeed, it could be a competitive game. Unfortunately, the Jags have also won games by 24, 29, 35, and 23 points this season. They have scored 31 or more in each of their past four games, and over 40 in two of those. The Giants have only scored more than 30 points once, and only then because of a 99-yard pick-6 on the last play of the game. Trevor Lawrence isn't necessarily playing any better this year than in the past. He's a QB that simultaneously makes great passes and puts the ball up for grabs, yet unlike in years past, he's cut down on the INTs while getting the TDs. Part of that may be due to 5'10" wide receiver Parker Washington (a 2023 6th-round pick), who had a breakout 2025 and is on pace for 1,000 yards. Running back Bhayshul Tuten, a 4th round 2025 pick, isn't quite in the Jahmyr Gibbs – Kenneth Walker class but he's not far below and is a missed tackle machine. A lot of the credit has to go to head coach Liam Coen, who also calls the plays and turned this team around as soon as he was hired. Lawrence, like most QBs, has trouble with pressure, but he is not too fazed by the blitz. Finding a way to disrupt his rhythm is a key to any chance the Giants may have. On defense, the Jaguars are strong at linebacker with fourth-round 2023 pick Ventrell Miller, one of the league's best (note how many mid-round picks the Jags have hit on), along with Foyesade Oluokun. They also put on a decent pass rush with Josh Hines-Allen, Travon Walker, and Dennis Gardeck. In the secondary, Travis Hunter is playing more like a No. 2 pick, having mostly given up his evening gig as a receiver. Are the Giants a serious playoff contender? This is the type of game they can use to make a statement against a team that is in the Super Bowl conversation. I think they'll put up a fight. I also don't think they're there yet. Pick : Jaguars Valentine's View I want to convince myself to pick the Giants to defeat the Jaguars. I really do. I just can't. The Jaguars are a team with justifiable Super Bowl ambitions . They are a well-rounded team with a high-powered offense, a very good defense, and one of the best field-goal kickers in the business in Cam Little. The Giants are a good team. They are resilient. They will give the Jaguars their best shot. Maybe, just maybe, it will be good enough to pull off an upset that would go a long way toward ensuring that the Giants make the playoffs. I just can't pick them to do it.

away.headline: Jaguars-Giants Injury Report: Bhayshul Tuten's Status Once Again Takes Top Focus
away.blurb: The Jaguars had 11 players carry either a limited or did-not-participate designation into Thursday's practice. Some names, like center Robert Hainsey's DNP situation due to a knee injury, were expected. But there was one change to Thursday's injury report that will trump all other names: Bhayshul Tuten, who was downgraded to a non-participant in practice after practicing in a limited fashion on Wednesday, which now creates quite the injury development to monitor before the Jaguars play the New York Giants in Week 11 on Sunday afternoon. Jaguars head coach Liam Coen has said in recent days that he has been pleased with Tuten's performances and toughness over the last two weeks. Add this to the fact that he played the last few weeks without a full week of practice, and it is hard to imagine Tuten sitting this one out, even if his injury will now come even more into focus. The Jaguars also had the following players listed as limited on Thursday: Jaguars-Giants Injury Report: Bhayshul Tuten's Status Once Again Takes Top Focus Skip to main content SI.COM JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- We are at that point of the season where injury reports closer resemble CVS receipts, and the Jaguars' Thursday injury report certainly checks that box. Tuten's status is a key one to watch any week, but especially in Week 11 when the Jaguars' running game is supposed to be pivotal against a blitz-happy Giants front that will test the Jaguars in the trenches. Tuten has played in each of the last two games despite practicing just once in those two weeks, and the Jaguars clearly did not feel like Tuten couldn't handle the bulk of the carries when he got 26 carries against the Titans on Sunday. “Obviously, last year being in a supplemental role, and I thought he was tough last year in some of the runs that he had where he just would kind of get whacked pretty good, get up and continue to play," Coen said on Wednesday. "To carry the load that he took this past week with 26 carries and play the amount of snaps he played still not quite 100%. I think the guy is probably mentally and physically tougher than I would've maybe imagined in ways." The smart bet would be to prepare for Tuten to play, but that does not mean this will not be a situation to monitor. It is such a key injury to watch in large part because the Jaguars have leaned on Tuten significantly over the course of the season. The second-year running back is arguably one of the three most important players on the offense alongside Trevor Lawrence and Parker Washington, and he has vastly outproduced the rest of the Jaguars' running back room. This is a big one, just like each game is a big one. But unless something changes on Friday, Tuten still should be considered a key part of Sunday's game. This doesn't come as a surprise when you take into account that head coach Liam Coen had already stated that the veteran hog molly won't be available against New York. home.headline: Giants Cam Skattebo Reveals Backflip Celebration's Future After Aidan Hutchinson's Knee Injury
home.blurb: Cam Skattebo is retiring the backflip. The New York Giants' running back said he will no longer do his signature celebration after seeing Detroit Lions' pass-rusher Aidan Hutchinson tear his ACL during a sack celebration on Sunday. "It's hard to see," Skattebo told reporters Monday. "I'm saying yeah [no more backflips]. Mentally, I'm like, 'I'm not doing that.' That ain't going to happen to me." He did add that he might bring back the backflip "if we go to the playoffs or something," but acknowledged that Hutchinson "didn't think about [the risk] either, and it happened." You have to think folks with the Giants' organization were jumping for joy—backflipping for joy, even—after hearing Skattebo's comments on the matter.
