LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin predict this weekend's top games Getty Images Last week in the NFL was full of drama. The Cleveland Browns came back from down 17-0 to defeat the Houston Texans , while Kirk Cousins was victorious in his first game back with the Minnesota Vikings . The San Francisco 49ers and Dallas Cowboys put up 86 total points in Arlington, and the Cincinnati Bengals blew out Aaron Rodgers and the Pittsburgh Steelers on "Sunday Night Football." This week there's more. Fernando Mendoza will make the first road start of his career against an aggressive Denver Broncos defense, the Detroit Lions will begin life without Aidan Hutchinson at home against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers , and the Vikings will play the 49ers in Mexico City in what could go down as one of the best primetime matchups of the entire season. There are many, many massive spreads in the NFL this week! Which teams should you pick in Week 11, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Nov. 18 over at DraftKings Sportsbook. Indianapolis Colts at Houston Texans (-12.5) (TNF) Dajani (Texans -12.5): I would typically lean toward a huge underdog like this in a divisional game, but two factors have me leaning the other way. One, Daniel Jones threw for just 108 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions last week against the Miami Dolphins . They were starting a quarterback that had never played in the NFL, yet only lost by two points. Jones has been terrible. He's turned the ball over an NFL-high 15 times and has the worst record in primetime by any quarterback since 1970 at 1-16. Additionally, the Texans allowed the Browns to come back from down 17-0 and win their meeting last week, which I imagine has this Texans team seeing red. C.J. Stroud and Co. are better than their 3-6 record indicates. They even beat the Jacksonville Jaguars earlier this season. I think the large number is justified. … Prediction: Texans 27, Colts 14 Dubin (Colts +12.5): I just don't think the Texans should be favored by 12.5 points over anybody. … Prediction: Texans 23, Colts 13 Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Detroit Lions (-7) Dajani (Buccaneers +7): Jahmyr Gibbs leads the NFL in rushing yards this season with 1,000, while the Buccaneers allow the fewest rushing yards per game (79.2). The Bucs also lead the NFL in rushing offense and in takeaways with 21. With the Buccaneers coming off their bye week and the Lions coming off an international trip that cost them Aidan Hutchinson for the season, I'm leaning toward Tampa Bay with the points. The Bucs are 4-1 against the spread in their last five games, but keep an eye on the quarterback situation over the next 24 hours. … Prediction: Lions 24, Buccaneers 21 Dubin (Lions -7): The Bucs likely playing this game without Baker Mayfield pushed me in this direction. Jalon Daniels is fine, but I don't expect the passing game to be able to do much here. The Bucs base the entire offense around the run anyway, but the Lions are actually pretty tough to run on. That could change without Aidan Hutchinson, obviously, but I don't think it will change enough for Tampa's offense to keep pace with what the Lions are likely to do. … Prediction: Lions 24, Buccaneers 16 Las Vegas Raiders at Denver Broncos (-10) Dajani (Broncos -10): I don't think Fernando Mendoza wins his second career start in an environment like Mile High, but can he cover the double-digit spread? Denver has won just one game by double digits this season, back in Week 7 against the Arizona Cardinals . The Las Vegas Raiders, on the other hand, have covered in four straight divisional games for the first time since 2022. The Broncos are coming off their bye week and have scored at least 26 points in each of their last three games. Bo Nix has also thrown multiple touchdowns in back-to-back games. The Raiders are tied for the worst scoring defense in the NFL this year with 28.9 points allowed per game, so I think the Broncos could reach 30 points this week. That could make it tough for Mendoza to cover the spread. He's actually the first rookie quarterback to ever face both of the previous season's No. 1 seeds in his first two career starts. … Prediction: Broncos 30, Raiders 17 Dubin (Raiders +10): The Broncos have seven wins this year, and six of them are by one score. The only team they beat by more than seven points is the Cardinals. I reserve the right to change this pick if Brock Bowers is out and Fernando Mendoza just doesn't have anyone at all to throw the ball to, but otherwise the Broncos just don't seem like a team capable of blowing out an opponent that has actually played fairly well this year. … Prediction: Broncos 21, Raiders 17 Jacksonville Jaguars (-6) at New York Giants Dajani ( Giants +6): No one is debating that the Jaguars are not one of the best teams in the NFL, but they haven't exactly been tested recently. They blew out the hapless Colts, had no problem with Joe Fagnano 's Baltimore Ravens and then dropped 40 points on the one-win Tennessee Titans . The Giants aren't Super Bowl contenders, but this is easily the best team Jacksonville has played in over the past month. I'm not going to take the Giants to win this game straight up, but I am leaning toward the six points. The Giants have an underrated defense that currently ranks No. 5 in the NFL in yards allowed per game (305.7), and J.J. McCarthy has the fifth-most yards per attempt (8.8) since his Giants debut in Week 5. Both of these teams are 6-3 ATS this season. Give me the Giants with a back-door cover. … Prediction: Jaguars 23, Giants 18 Dubin (Jaguars -6): Unlike the Broncos, the Jaguars have blown out everybody. Five of their seven wins have come by 17 points or more, including each of their last three games. The Giants are probably better than the Colts, Ravens and Titans, but I don't see them hanging with this Jacksonville offense — not with the Jags getting their new defensive stalwarts on the field for the first time since the trade deadline. ( Jessie Bates III and Jordan Davis sat out last week because they had yet to have their bye and the Jags had already taken theirs.) … Prediction: Jaguars 31, Giants 20 Minnesota Vikings vs. San Francisco 49ers (-3) (SNF in Mexico City) Dajani (49ers -3): The 49ers are coming off a ridiculous 46-40 win over the Cowboys, where they recorded the most total yards in a road game in franchise history (584) and averaged a whopping 9.4 yards per play. Brock Purdy's offense had three touchdowns of 65+ yards! Christian McCaffrey actually became the first running back in NFL history to record two 65-yard receiving touchdowns in a game. Obviously, the Vikings' defense is MUCH better than the Cowboys', but something you should know is that this game is in Mexico City. And both teams have prepared for it differently . The stadium the 49ers and Vikings will play in on Sunday is over 7,000 feet above sea level. So, the 49ers traveled to the U.S. Air Force Academy in Colorado Springs this week, which is at an elevation of 6,621 feet , to prepare. The Vikings, on the other hand, apparently built an altitude chamber so players can get familiar with "thinner air" before Sunday, but otherwise are seemingly pulling a Los Angeles Rams and just showing up on site the day before the game. The 49ers dominated the Rams in Australia in Week 1, 27-7, and part of that was because their travel plans were so much better. The 49ers have won and covered in four straight International games. … Prediction: 49ers 26, Vikings 20 Dubin (49ers -3): In a battle of a great offense against a great defense, I am usually going to lean toward the offensive side unless there's a really compelling reason in favor of the defensive-minded team. Kirk Cousins' ability to elevate the Vikings' own offense almost provides that reason, but it's not quite enough for me to get there. This San Francisco offense is too much of a well-oiled machine for me to pick against the Niners — even in a matchup with a defensive coordinator as crazy and as good as Brian Flores. … Prediction: 49ers 23, Vikings 17 Cincinnati Bengals (-6.5) at Washington Commanders (MNF) Dajani (Bengals -6.5): Before you think this is some easy pick to make just because of how hot the Bengals are, know that Cincy is 0-2-1 in its past three games against the Washington Commanders , who just upset the Giants in New York last week. Jayden Daniels ' coming-out party as a rookie actually came against the Bengals. Still, it's hard to go against my Super Bowl pick and my MVP pick this season. I did that the past two weeks. After a good Week 9 picking games, I was solid again in Week 10. I went 9-5 against the spread and 8-6 straight up. I'll take it. Two weeks in a row. Wow. The records after 10 weeks are now 95-54-1 straight up and 68-79-3 ATS. Climbing out of a huge hole, ATS has me now visibly seeing the .500 mark. Let's hope the hot streak stays as we move towards Thanksgiving. There are a ton of big spreads this week, so watch out. The dogs might be barking. All lines via DraftKings ; All times ET Miami Dolphins (+16.5) at Buffalo Bills Sunday, 1 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) Miami is playing consecutive road games after losing at Indianapolis, while the Bills are home for the first time after two road games. The Bills are playing better on defense in recent weeks against some lower-level quarterbacks. They get another one here in backup Kyle McCord . The Bills will score, as Josh Allen always plays well against Miami, but Miami stays around. Pick: Bills 31, Dolphins 19 New Orleans Saints (+11.5) at Chicago Bears Sunday, 1 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Bears are off a bye, while the Saints lost to the Panthers last week. Chicago is much improved on defense. With the Saints unable to run the ball, it will put a lot of pressure on Saints quarterback Tyler Shough . Caleb Williams will bounce back from his four-interception game last time out against Tampa Bay and will play well here. Bears take it. Pick: Bears 24, Saints 16 Tennessee Titans at Dallas Cowboys (-8.5) The Cowboys are bad on defense, but the Titans haven't exactly lit it up on offense. Cam Ward has played better as of late. Even so, look for the Cowboys offense to have a big day throwing it against a Tennessee defense that struggles against the pass. Dak Prescott will put up big numbers. Pick: Cowboys 37, Titans 23 Tampa Bay Buccaneers (+7) at Detroit Lions The issue here is whether Baker Mayfield will play for the Bucs. If not, they will have big problems. The Lions are back home after beating up the Patriots in Germany last week. The offense was dominant that day, but this Tampa Bay defense is playing well. That will keep them in the game, but the uncertainty at quarterback will be too much to overcome. Pick: Lions 22, Bucs 17 Arizona Cardinals at Kansas City Chiefs (-16.5) Carson Beck makes his first road start for the Cardinals and this is as tough as any place in the league to do so. The Chiefs are coming off an impressive road victory in which Patrick Mahomes threw five touchdown passes. The defense is third in the league in scoring. That will make for a tough day for this limited Arizona offense. Blowout. Pick: Chiefs 33, Cardinals 14 Pittsburgh Steelers (-4.5) at Philadelphia Eagles The Eagles are coming off a bye, while the Steelers are coming off a loss to division-rival Cincinnati. The Eagles are a shell of the team they were early in the season because of injuries and trades. This battle of Pennsylvania has lost some luster. Look for the Steelers to bounce back with a tough defensive effort against an undermanned offense, and Aaron Rodgers will play well. Pick: Steelers 26, Eagles 13 Baltimore Ravens (+2.5) at Carolina Panthers Both of these teams are in desperation mode when it comes to needing victories for the postseason. The Ravens lost at home Monday night to the previously winless Chargers and now have to head out on the road on a short week. That's tough. The Panthers played better defense last week against the Saints, which will help them here. Carolina wins it late, but it's close. Pick: Panthers 23, Ravens 22 New York Jets at Los Angeles Chargers (-3.5) Sunday, 4:05 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Chargers won for the first time on Monday night, beating the Ravens on the road. They actually showed some offensive life in that game. The Jets have defensive issues, which the Chargers can take advantage of here. Quarterback Geno Smith is banged up for the Jets, which could mean rookie Cade Klubnik makes his first NFL start. Look for the Chargers to take advantage if that is the case as they get to 2-8 behind another solid showing by the offense. Pick: Chargers 28, Jets 24 Las Vegas Raiders at Denver Broncos (-10) Sunday, 4:25 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) Fernando Mendoza will be making his first road start, which can be tough for a rookie. But it's also against a really good defense coming off a bye in a tough place to play. That's a real challenge. Look for the Broncos to get after him in this one. The Raiders ' defense isn't playing well, so maybe it's just what Bo Nix needs. Broncos big. Pick: Broncos 31, Raiders 14 Jacksonville Jaguars (-6) at New York Giants This is a big game for both teams. The Jaguars are 7-2 and playing as well as any team in the league. But they are playing consecutive road games against a Giants team pushing for a division title. This game will be decided by the Giants' defense against the Jaguars' offense. I think the Jaguars get the better of it. Look for them to run it well with Bhayshul Tuten . Pick: Jaguars 26, Giants 17 Minnesota Vikings at San Francisco 49ers (-3) In Mexico, Sunday, 8:20 p.m. on NBC (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) This is the best game of the week, featuring two of the NFC's best. The 49ers beat Dallas last week, while the Vikings beat the Packers in Kirk Cousins ' first game back with the team after being traded by the Raiders. This will be about the 49ers offense vs. Brian Flores' defense. I think Kyle Shanahan will get the best of it as the 49ers keep rolling. Big day for Christian McCaffrey running it. Pick: 49ers 23, Vikings 16 Cincinnati Bengals at Washington Commanders (+6.5) Monday, 8:15 p.m. on ESPN, ABC (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Bengals are rolling on offense as Joe Burrow pushes toward the MVP. The Commanders have had problems against the pass, ranking 31st in the league, which has to have Burrow and the offense ready to go. Jayden Daniels won't keep up, but it's close. The Bengals keep rolling. Pick: Bengals 34, Commanders 30 Indianapolis Colts (+12.5) at Houston Texans Thursday, 8:15 p.m. on Amazon Prime If the Texans are to have any chance of making the playoffs, they have to win this one. The Colts are pretty much done, but they beat Miami last week. Daniel Jones struggled in that one, but the Texans' defense has really struggled. Look for the Colts to hang around here, but the Texans will win it. picks.headline: Sportsbook Insiders: Insights on Vikings vs. 49ers Odds for Sunday Night Football; Kirk Cousins Impact
picks.blurb: Sportsbook Insiders: Insights on Vikings vs. 49ers Odds for Sunday Night Football; Kirk Cousins Impact Skip to main content BUY THE ISSUE PREDICTION MARKETS Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code Fanatics Sportsbook Promo Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Rainbet Promo Code Stake Promo Code College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code Novig Promo Code Underdog Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI Minnesota Vikings quarterback Kirk Cousins has transformed the NFC playoff picture since being traded from Las Vegas to Minnesota at the trade deadline, and that’s set up a very interesting Sunday Night Football matchup in Week 11. The Vikings are set to face the San Francisco 49ers in a neutral site game in Mexico City, and there are a ton of playoff implications at stake. Not only are the Vikings battling for first place in the NFC North, but a win over San Fran would give Minnesota a legit shot at the No. 1 seed in the conference. A Cousins trade materialized for Minnesota after back-to-back losses to Detroit and Buffalo where Kyler Murray (against Detroit) and Carson Wentz (against Buffalo) showed that they simply aren’t playing quarterback at a high enough level for the Vikings to win a Super Bowl. That sentiment has changed in the futures market, as the Vikings are now priced around 15/1 to win it all after an upset win over Green Bay in Week 10. The odds for that game shifted in a big way after Cousins was acquired, as the same goes for Week 11 against San Francisco. Sports Illustrated spoke to several oddsmakers this week to see just how much the Cousins’ acquisition has changed the Vikings’ outlook in this Sunday Night matchup. How Much Kirk Cousins Impacts Vikings vs. 49ers Odds for NFL Week 11 The Vikings opened as 3.5-point underdogs in Week 11 after their win over Green Bay, but that line has continued to move towards the Vikings, settling at 3. While that’s a minor move, there’s a chance this line would have been set as far as 49ers -7 if Murray or Wentz was under center on Sunday night. “Well, if the quarterback play continued to go the way it was before Cousins arrived, the Vikings would have been close to a touchdown underdog, rather than a field goal underdog,” Johnny Avello, Director of Race and Sports Operations for DraftKings Sportsbook , told Sports Illustrated. That’s at least a four-point swing in favor of the 49ers, though not every book had that price. BetMGM and FanDuel both told Sports Illustrated that the spread would likely be close to four or five. “Not too much believe it or not, probably was about a point or so move,” Christian Cipollini, Senior Trading Manager at BetMGM , told Sports Illustrated. The reason being is there isn't a major gap between Cousins and Murray. The main reason for this spread being close is the strength of the defense. Both QBs are capable, it helps Minnesota's future odds more because if one gets injured they have a capable backup to come in.” It’s interesting to hear about different pricing across the industry, as Fanatics has a much different grade – but similar to DraftKings – when it comes to the Murray vs. Cousins debate: “We opened up a lookahead line on the day of trade deadline day, it was plus seven,” Ty Gour, Sports Trader at Fanatics Sportsbook , told Sports Illustrated. “And now the Vikings are three-point dogs, just to give you an idea of how highly we rate Kirk Cousins versus Murray or Wentz.” In his first start with the Vikings, Cousins threw for 207 yards, two scores and one pick, and he has 22 touchdown passes in the 2026 season. There’s no doubt that this Vikings team – which has the No. 2 defense in EPA/Play in 2026 – has a much better chance of competing with San Fran’s No. 1 offense with Cousins calling the shots. What Would the Vikings vs. 49ers Spread Be in San Francisco? This game is also unusual because of the neutral site aspect. While this is technically a home game for San Francisco, it likely would be favored by more Levi’s Stadium in Santa Clara. Still, Avello explained that home field doesn’t matter as much as it used to when DraftKings sets the spread for games. “ The Niners playing at home – there's a misconception with home-field advantage,” Avello said. When you look at it across the league, it's only a couple of points. Some teams get a little stronger, and a lot of it has to do with weather. So, the Niners would have been only maybe another point and a half at home, so maybe the line would have been 4.5.” San Francisco is a perfect 5-0 at home in the 2026 season, so it’ll be interesting to see if Kyle Shanahan’s team can hold up on a neutral field. The 49ers (8-1) are looking to maintain their lead in the NFC and NFC West, but a loss to Minnesota would bring it back down into the same playing field with other two-loss teams like Chicago and Detroit. As the betting lines open for this heavyweight clash, the Vikings are starting the week as a slight underdog for what is, at least nominally, a San Francisco home game. Skol! Chat live throughout the game Enjoy fewer ads Jump easily between communities Comment and post faster Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android . Our friends at the FanDuel Sportsbook have opened the betting lines for this week, and the Vikings have started as a three-point underdog to the Niners. The over/under for this one has started at 46.5 points. The Vikings snapped their two-game losing streak this past Sunday at Lambeau Field, pasting the Green Bay Packers by a score of 30-10 to complete a sweep of the Border Battle for the 2026 season. The defense was dominant, sacking Jordan Love eight times and forcing three of the four turnovers committed by the Packers (the fourth came on special teams). But the big story was the Vikings' offense and the return of Kirk Cousins, whom the Vikings acquired at the trade deadline on Tuesday, arrived in Minnesota on Wednesday, and started on Sunday, making him the first player since at least 1950 to start games at quarterback for different teams in consecutive weeks. Cousins' last start for his former team, the Las Vegas Raiders, came against these same 49ers, who come into this game tied for the league's best record at 8-1. Like the Vikings, the Niners got their season off to a 6-0 start before seeing their first loss, a 29-20 defeat to the Atlanta Falcons in Week 7. After the bye, they came back to beat Cousins and the Raiders by a score of 38-17, and this past Sunday they had a back-and-forth battle with the Dallas Cowboys that saw them eventually emerge with a 46-40 victory at Jerryworld. Brock Purdy is on the short list of potential MVP candidates for this season, and he showed why against the Cowboys, completing 22-of-28 passes for 389 yards and three touchdowns, two of which came on long passes to Christian McCaffrey, who had 161 receiving yards on the day. This matchup looks to be another matchup of a very strong offense facing off against Brian Flores' #1 defensive squad. Unlike what we saw when the Vikings faced the Bills on Monday Night, however, now it appears that the Vikings have the offense to actually allow their defense to have a bit of a rest and not allow them to get worn down late in the game. For the fourth consecutive week, the Vikings will go into a game as an underdog, ladies and gentlemen. What do you think about that? Let us know in the comments!

picks.headline: Justin Jefferson Given Bold Superlative in Vikings vs. 49ers Preview
picks.blurb: Justin Jefferson Given Bold Superlative in Vikings vs. 49ers Preview - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football Texans cruise on TNF Curt Cignetti slams report Trump pardons Pete Rose Puka Nacua suspended 3 games 'GTA 6' impacts sports Justin Jefferson Given Bold Superlative in Vikings vs. 49ers Preview (Brad Rempel-Imagn Images) Joey Hickey · Roundtable Sports Fri, November 20, 2026 at 12:00 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Minnesota Vikings (7-2) made a statement last Sunday. The Vikings went out and defeated the Green Bay Packers (6-4) in Lambeau Field, 30-10. If you stopped paying attention two weeks ago, you're probably wondering how that happened. In short, the Vikings traded for quarterback Kirk Cousins and kept its defensive dominance intact. The result? A complete dismantling of a rival that has had the upper hand for the better part of the rivalry. Ahead for the Vikings is the team's biggest test of the season. Minnesota will take on the best team in the NFC. They will have to do so in Mexico City. Steve Silverman of Athlon Sports discussed how the Vikings could make an even bigger statement in their game against the San Francisco 49ers in Mexico City. To do so, they could use a big game from star wide receiver Justin Jefferson. Here's some of what Silverman had to say on Jefferson's effect on the matchup. "There was no player who needed to see improvement at the QB position more than Jefferson. Kyler Murray and Carson Wentz failed to get the ball to Jefferson in the first half of the season, but that immediately changed with Cousins under center. Jefferson was targeted 13 times in that game and he caught 9 passes for 74 yards. He needs to do even more in this game. Jefferson needs at least one big play in this game to help his team play effectively on offense. Jefferson caught a 97-yard TD pass the last time the Vikings played the Niners in Week 2 of the 2024 season. That play stunned San Francisco and the Vikings were able to dictate the pace. A big play early in the game from Jefferson could give Minnesota the edge in this game." Cousins' emergence opened up a world of possibilities for the Vikings offense, but one of the big changes could involve Jefferson regaining the production he had in Cousins' first stint with Minnesota. We saw flashes of what things could look like against the Packers. Nobody is going to confuse the Vikings for one of the best operating offenses in the NFL, but a couple of explosive plays to Jefferson could mean the difference between a narrow Vikings loss and Minnesota building a two-score lead that its defense won't squander. We'll keep an eye on how the Vikings utilize Jefferson in the consequential matchup on Sunday.

away.headline: Vikings-49ers injury updates: Are reinforcements coming for game in Mexico City?
away.blurb: On Thursday, Minnesota Vikings linebacker Blake Cashman practiced fully for the second straight day, putting him on track to return from the concussion protocol for Sunday night’s game against the San Francisco 49ers . Cashman, the Vikings’ leading tackler who missed last week’s win in Green Bay, resumed his full workload this week in practices after missing last week’s win in Green Bay. Quarterback Kyler Murray (hamstring) and receiver Jordan Addison (thumb) were the only players held out Thursday. Hockenson, who has been limited in practice, said he’s “feeling good” and trying to play against the 49ers. He missed the Packers game due to wrist and chest injuries suffered in the Nov. 9 loss to Buffalo. Outside linebacker Andrew Van Ginkel and cornerback Isaiah Rodgers were limited Thursday due to quad injuries. San Francisco got receiver Mike Evans (Achilles) and linebacker Dre Greenlaw (neck) back at Thursday’s practice; both players took limited reps. Tight end T.J. Hockenson (wrist), receiver Jauan Jennings and defensive lineman Tyrion Ingram-Dawkins (ankle) also returned to practice this week. Jennings, the former 49ers starter who declined a trade back to San Francisco last month, has missed two games because of a calf strain. “It’s going to be a boost to get Jauan back,” coach Kevin O’Connell said Wednesday. “We know he’s going to be competing this week considering the opponent.” ©2026 The Minnesota Star Tribune. away.headline: Vikings-49ers game marks return to Mexico City, though the NFL never truly left
away.blurb: Many fans will no doubt view Sunday's matchup between the San Francisco 49ers and Minnesota Vikings as marking the NFL's return to Mexico . "I fell in love with the 49ers in the mid-80s because of Joe Montana. I've attended every game held in Mexico, and it's great that they're back," said Octavio Zúñiga, a 50-year-old fan. "Last time (in 2022), they came out carrying the Mexican flag as they entered the stadium. That commitment to the Mexican fan base is truly appreciated." November 19, 2026 / 8:39 AM CST / CBS Minnesota The reality is, the league never truly left. Although Mexico last hosted a regular-season game in 2022, the league's growth in the country has been steady, according to Arturo Olivé, managing director of NFL Mexico. Over the past 18 years, the league's domestic fan base has surged from roughly 10 million to 40 million, according to the NFL. "We have grown significantly over these years thanks to the constant, continuous, daily work of our team," Olivé said. "Eighteen years ago, we chose our battles and focused our attention on the specific areas we needed to improve in order to expand our fan base." In Mexico, the NFL trails only soccer — the national sport — in total fans. The game's popularity is no coincidence; American football is as much a part of Mexican sports tradition as soccer, boxing, and lucha libre. The Mexico game will be the last of the nine international NFL games played this season, a league record. To expand its reach, NFL Mexico invested heavily in flag football, which has steadily gained traction and now boasts roughly 4 million players nationwide. While impressive, Olivé acknowledges that in a nation of more than 130 million people, there is still vast room for growth. To accelerate adoption, the league signed an agreement with the National Commission of Physical Culture and Sport (CONADE) to expand the sport across public schools. "With 4 million children in the program, we are barely scratching the surface. Forty million fans in Mexico is a lot, but there are still another 80 or 90 million people we could reach," Olivé said. CONADE, the agency that oversees Mexico's federal sports budget, is eager to promote flag football ahead of its debut as an Olympic sport at the 2028 Los Angeles Games. Mexico's women's national team has already secured an Olympic berth. "We believe this alliance turns schools into spaces for participation, well-being and talent development," said Rommel Pacheco, general director of CONADE. "We want more girls, boys, and young people to play an accessible and inclusive sport." Olivé noted that initiatives such as flag football and Play 60 have been particularly effective at drawing women to the game. Today, women account for 47% of Mexico's 40 million NFL fans. home.headline: Vikings-49ers game marks return to Mexico City, though the NFL never truly left
home.blurb: Many fans will no doubt view Sunday's matchup between the San Francisco 49ers and Minnesota Vikings as marking the NFL's return to Mexico . "I fell in love with the 49ers in the mid-80s because of Joe Montana. I've attended every game held in Mexico, and it's great that they're back," said Octavio Zúñiga, a 50-year-old fan. "Last time (in 2022), they came out carrying the Mexican flag as they entered the stadium. That commitment to the Mexican fan base is truly appreciated." November 19, 2026 / 8:39 AM CST / CBS Minnesota The reality is, the league never truly left. Although Mexico last hosted a regular-season game in 2022, the league's growth in the country has been steady, according to Arturo Olivé, managing director of NFL Mexico. Over the past 18 years, the league's domestic fan base has surged from roughly 10 million to 40 million, according to the NFL. "We have grown significantly over these years thanks to the constant, continuous, daily work of our team," Olivé said. "Eighteen years ago, we chose our battles and focused our attention on the specific areas we needed to improve in order to expand our fan base." In Mexico, the NFL trails only soccer — the national sport — in total fans. The game's popularity is no coincidence; American football is as much a part of Mexican sports tradition as soccer, boxing, and lucha libre. The Mexico game will be the last of the nine international NFL games played this season, a league record. To expand its reach, NFL Mexico invested heavily in flag football, which has steadily gained traction and now boasts roughly 4 million players nationwide. While impressive, Olivé acknowledges that in a nation of more than 130 million people, there is still vast room for growth. To accelerate adoption, the league signed an agreement with the National Commission of Physical Culture and Sport (CONADE) to expand the sport across public schools. "With 4 million children in the program, we are barely scratching the surface. Forty million fans in Mexico is a lot, but there are still another 80 or 90 million people we could reach," Olivé said. CONADE, the agency that oversees Mexico's federal sports budget, is eager to promote flag football ahead of its debut as an Olympic sport at the 2028 Los Angeles Games. Mexico's women's national team has already secured an Olympic berth. "We believe this alliance turns schools into spaces for participation, well-being and talent development," said Rommel Pacheco, general director of CONADE. "We want more girls, boys, and young people to play an accessible and inclusive sport." Olivé noted that initiatives such as flag football and Play 60 have been particularly effective at drawing women to the game. Today, women account for 47% of Mexico's 40 million NFL fans. That culminated in an absolute whooping of the Pittsburgh Steelers at home on Sunday Night Football that wasn't even as close as the 20-point win made it seem. Now they are taking their show on the road to play the Washington Commanders in their house on Monday Night Football. Joe Burrow is 0-2 so far in his career against the Commanders, but that comes with some pretty big caveats. The first loss was the game in which he injured his knee midway through the game as a rookie. The other loss came in an absolute monster of a shootout where the Bengals defense did not stop the Commanders or Jayden Daniels a single time in 2024, with the game ending 38-33. That would not be the first time Burrow would helm a losing team despite putting up more than 30 points over the next few seasons. These teams are drastically different as the Cincinnati defense has had a major overhaul, and Washington is far from the team it was during Daniels' rookie season. There is no doubt Daniels is a talented quarterback, but the Commanders themselves seem to be a very average to below-average team that needs a combination of home run hits on offense and a handful of turnovers to spark a win. Meanwhile, Burrow, Ja'Marr Chase, and Tee Higgins are giving their best impressions of the Colts' offense during Peyton Manning's heyday by trusting their quarterback to put up points with his top weapons over a balanced attack. That has led to four straight games of four touchdowns for Burrow, which ties a record set by Manning. The real x-factor here will be the Bengals defense. Will the version we have seen since the Madrid game against the Atlanta Falcons show up that has been able to contain opposing offenses that tried to test their linebackers and safeties? Or will the young players at those positions allow a few too many big plays? Here is how the oddsmakers and experts feel about the game. The Bengals are currently 6.5-point road favorites against the Commanders, according to FanDuel Sportsbook . It really is a fairly big deal when a road team gets almost a touchdown advantage over a home team. It clearly shows that there is a step between where these two teams are currently at. The point total is set at 53.5 is the second highest of the week. That is fair because even when this team has faced teams like the Tennessee Titans, they have given up opportunities to score. 10 of ESPN's 11 experts are going with the Bengals CBS Sports has all seven experts taking Cincinnati to win All five of NFL.com's experts are expecting the Bengals to extend their win streak to six games NFL Pick Watch — which takes into account picks from across the web — has Cincinnati receiving 99% of the picks for this game. Cincy Jungle Pick I think this team has really turned a corner as far as this defense is concerned. The young linebacker duo of Demetrius Knight and Barrett Carter have grown enough to prove to be a competent — maybe not the most consistent — duo. That is the level of play this defense needs when the defensive line led by Boye Mafe and Dexter Lawrence is able to get penetration. We will have to see how well they contain Daniels, who can really cause some damage by extending plays with his legs. All of that more or less will determine how much the Commanders lose by. Washington has no way of slowing down or throwing off this offense. The Bengals are getting into at least the 30s. Can the Commanders keep pace? Final Score: Bengals 45, Commanders 25 Who Dey! home.headline: Re-grading Commanders’ 2026 NFL Draft picks at midseason as Sonny Styles surges
home.blurb: Re-grading Commanders’ 2026 NFL Draft picks at midseason as Sonny Styles surges Skip to main content News The Washington Commanders embarked on a mini-youth movement this offseason. For this plan to work, general manager Adam Peters needed immediate returns from his 2026 NFL Draft class . Peters went away from aging veterans chasing a ring , replacing them with younger free agents coming off their rookie contracts. And even though Washington didn't have many draft picks after some blockbuster trades, the selections made were largely well received. That was something. But it would count for nothing if they didn't show up in a competitive regular-season setting. Looking at how things are shaping up at midseason, there have been far more positives than negatives with this group. Almost all have seen some action, and with undrafted rookie kicker Drew Stevens , the Commanders may have found their solution to a long-running problem. This is just the start. They are only going to get better with more experience, and the fact that most have received playing time so far will only serve them well. And for one or two, their status as long-term pieces of Washington's ambitious project is already secure. With that in mind, we re-graded the Commanders' 2026 NFL Draft class after nine games. Re-grading the Washington Commanders' 2026 NFL Draft at the midseason point Washington Commanders quarterback Athan Kaliakmanis | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Commanders drafted Athan Kaliakmanis Commanders drafted Athan Kaliakmanis A few eyebrows were raised when the Washington Commanders used their final selection on quarterback Athan Kaliakmanis. Jayden Daniels is the franchise player, and Marcus Mariota re-signed as the backup. Fans wondered whether the incoming rookie would even make the team, but those concerns are gone now. Daniels dislocated his elbow again . That moved Kaliakmanis into a backup role, and when Mariota sustained a sprained MCL early in Washington's international game against the Indianapolis Colts, the former Rutgers gunslinger was thrown into the fire. It was a daunting proposition. But even though Kaliakmanis went through some unavoidable growing pains, he also flashed some intriguing qualities that could become something more over time. Kaliakmanis saw the field well. He was aggressive, showcasing velocity and conviction with his throws. It wasn't perfect, and things moved a little too fast at times, but it could have been a lot worse. The best way for young players to learn is through live-fire reps. Kaliakmanis probably won't see the field again this season, but this experience will have done wonders for his overall development. This is a development project, of course. Kaliakmanis is the third-string option, which is fine for now. But a situation could emerge where he evolves into Daniels' primary backup when the 2027 season begins. To understand what their pass rush moves are and all the different front looks that we can see. I know that they're not satisfied either, but those guys are lights out." "We've already had all the confidence in the world," Burrow said on Sunday about the team's execution and improvement following a 2-2 start. "This happened on Wednesday, Thursday, and Friday practices, and the rest took care of itself on Sunday. I think we all had a good feeling about what was going to happen today, and we went out and made it happen ... We just kept getting better — just grinding at practice and improving, (and) improving through meetings. We've got great coaches that make adjustments and try to put us in really good positions to go and make plays, and right now we are."
